articles.title: 10 Unusual jobs in football - BBC Bitesize
articles.summary: What are some of the lesser known jobs in football? BBC Bitesize Careers finds out!
articles.body:
Player, manager, referee, coach – if you were asked to name a job in football, we reckon you might be able to reply quickly with one of these. But what about private chef, bodyguard, or barber? These are just three of the many, many, slightly more unusual roles that exist in the game. After all, someone has to make sure players eat well, are kept safe, and captured creatively for the ‘gram, while fans also want to have an amazing match-day experience.

BBC Bitesize Careers caught up with author and creator of Jamie Johnson Dan Freedman, who like many people finds himself working in the world of football without being a player on the pitch. He’s written the book 50 Ways Into Football: Dream Jobs on and Off the Pitch and we couldn’t help but get stuck in and select a few of our favourites.

Take a scroll through the carousel and see how many of these roles you already know…

images.caption: Image caption, Bodyguard For some of the games most elite players, security is an absolute priority such is the level of stardom. Take Lionel Messi for example, he has a full-time bodyguard. Yassine Cheuko, who has a background in Mixed Martial Arts, is never far from the Argentinian player’s side! Job requirements: A good level of fitness, eyes on the back of your head.

Image caption, Stadium Announcer Keeping the vibe going on match days can be a tricky task, especially if the home team isn’t performing at their best. But when it comes to a fan’s match-day experience, away from the action the pitch, the stadium announcer is often the unknown star of the show. From pre-match hype-building, to making sure everyone know which players are being substituted, it’s all in the day job. Job requirements: A commanding voice and a decent playlist!!

Image caption, Tournament Organiser Tournaments like the UEFA Champions League capture the imagination of fans around Europe and beyond, it’s where the best meet the best. But logistically these tournaments are huge operations, from scheduling to staffing, planning epic ceremonies to keeping on top of player appearances. It all falls on the shoulders of the often unspoken about Tournament Organiser. Job Requirements: An encyclopaedic knowledge of the tournament, some space in your passport for stamps.

Image caption, Freestyle Footballer If tactics and formations aren’t for you but you reckon you’ve still got some impressive talent when it comes to ball skills, football freestyling might be for you. It’s a continually growing area of the game, complete with annual world championships. Great Britain’s Liv Cooke is a former world champ! Job Requirements: Top tekkerz, and then some more top tekkerz.

Image caption, Club Photographer Imagine getting to be in the dressing room when your team gets the big win, or when a new player arrives at the club, capturing the moment for fans can often fall to the club’s own photographer. Always ready, with camera in hand, they need to expect the unexpected, including turning from being the photographer to being the subject of the photograph. Just ask Martin Ødegaard. Job Requirements: A good knowledge of the ‘gram, plenty of charged batteries.

Image caption, Football Video Game Designer Footie video games are big business. Keeping them as accurate and representative to the game on the pitch is vitally important for the people that design and work on making them (and of course for the people who play them). We know the team at EA Sports will be busy doing all of that right now, their next release is expected to drop November this year. Job Requirements: An eye for detail, a willingness to spend a lot of time playing and testing video games.

Image caption, Barber/Hair Stylist From Cole Palmer’s high fade, to Marcus Rashford’s latest braid design, it’s often claimed that when players feel and look their best, they play their best too. Whether that’s exactly true or not we’ll leave it up to you to decide. But when it comes to looking sharp, or trying out something a little different on top, one thing is for sure, footballers all have their go-to guy or girl! Job Requirements: Some creative clippers and good chat for when the client is in the chair.

Image caption, Private Jet Pilot From jetting off to world cups in far flung locations to needing to make dramatic transfer deadline day journeys footballers cover the miles, and not always on the team bus. There’s often a need to fly, and where there’s a private plane, there’s a private pilot, like this uniformed chap who flew Granit Xhaxa to sign for Sunderland FC in 2025. We reckon it's some way to see the world. Job Requirements: Solid flying skills and a professional attitude, no head in the clouds here.

articles.title: Vallecas ya está listo para la vuelta de su Rayo
articles.standfirst: El estadio franjirrojo volverá a acoger un encuentro de liga más de cuatro meses después
articles.summary: El estadio franjirrojo volverá a acoger un encuentro de liga más de cuatro meses después
articles.body: Y 146 días después, LaLiga vuelve a Vallecas. El Rayo Vallecano jugará ante el Athletic de Bilbao su primer partido oficial en casa de la temporada, después de la disputa del Trofeo de Vallecas que acabó en derrota para el cuadro franjirrojo y en protestas. Después de un verano con muchos cambios y de un comienzo de temporada inestable, vuelve la competición doméstica al barrio más grande de toda Europa. El cuadro franjirrojo disputó las tres primeras jornadas como local (Alavés, Racing y Espanyol), pero no en su estadio. Todo comenzó con una convocatoria a los medios por parte de la Consejería de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte para hablar sobre el feudo franjirrojo. Ninguno de los que se encontraba allí se esperó aquella sorpresa: la retirada de la concesión al Rayo y la inhabilitación del estadio debido a que en la primera auditoría que se realizó se detectó “una situación que comprometía la seguridad y operatividad del recinto”. Todo ocurrió el 28 de julio de 2026 y lo peor aún estaba por llegar. La Comunidad de Madrid se personó en el Estadio de Vallecas y el club no le dejó entrar. En cambio, sí que se vieron operarios trabajando en la limpieza de las gradas del estadio, en el mantenimiento del césped y demás necesidades. El 4 de agosto, los técnicos de la Comunidad pudieron entrar, mientras tanto seguían las obras de restauración. Todas las miradas apuntaban a ese día 20 de agosto. Fecha en la que el Rayo jugaba la segunda jornada liguera, ante el Deportivo Alavés, esta vez en casa. El 17 de agosto, la Comunidad de Madrid rechazó la cautelar solicitada por el Rayo Vallecano para que pudiera jugar su encuentro en casa. Ante la negativa de esta petición, el club franjirrojo solicitó a LaLiga el aplazamiento del encuentro del Alavés, dos días antes de su disputa. Este ‘tira y afloja’ entre instituciones lleva ocurriendo desde entonces y en todos y cada uno de los encuentros que se deberían de haber jugado en Vallecas. Una afición totalmente desesperada y el Rayo Vallecano jugando en Butarque. A finales de agosto comenzó la segunda auditoría y el 14 de septiembre la Comunidad de Madrid levantó la suspensión cautelar del Estadio de Vallecas. Tan solo un día antes del encuentro de la jornada 6 ante el Espanyol. El nuevo informe concluyó que “las instalaciones inspeccionadas se encuentran operativas y en condiciones adecuadas para su funcionamiento ordinario”, gracias a “una mejora material y documental muy significativa respecto de la situación descrita en la auditoría inicial”, según el informe de la Consejería. Los operarios no han parado de trabajar en las deficiencias desde entonces hasta la puesta en orden de la mayoría de los elementos de la sede franjirroja. Sin embargo, tal y como quedó constancia en el Trofeo de Vallecas, las mejoras no son suficientes y todavía queda mucho trabajo por hacer. Además, el club aún tiene que solventar ocho puntos de diferentes áreas del estadio para que no se le extinga la concesión por incumplimiento del acuerdo. No obstante, la última auditoría corroboró que ya no se observan cables colgando por las paredes y cuadros abiertos. Las cajas están cerradas y los conductores eléctricos canalizados. Faltan documentos sobre un transformador y mediciones y documentación sobre cuadros, circuitos y canalizaciones. También se han subsanado deficiencias en los medios de PCI (Protección contra Incendios). Se ha comprobado su funcionamiento y están señalizados. Al club le queda demostrar que tres sistemas de detección y alarma de incendios funcionan (sala de árbitros, restaurante y cocina) y enviar informes sobre el abastecimiento y bocas de incendios. También se ha renovado la seguridad de las instalaciones térmicas y de gas, pero aún falta completar la medición y documentación de caudales de aire en vestuarios, zonas húmedas, salas de prensa, UCO y oficinas y completar el inventario de equipos térmicos y de climatización y el cálculo de la potencia térmica nominal instalada. Se han limpiado instalaciones como el área de restauración o los sótanos. Lugares totalmente abandonados que presentaban gran cantidad de basura y elementos inutilizados. En el exterior del estadio se han pintado los pasos para minusválidos. En este caso, el club debe presentar aún un informe sobre la evacuación del estadio y la separación de la afición visitante y la segunda auditoría señaló que gran parte de los equipamientos que dan servicio y suministro al estadio tienen una antigüedad relevante. El Rayo Vallecano también presentó la documentación que le requirió inicialmente la Consejería y que, por su ausencia, se obligó a suspender la actividad en el estadio. El club aportó analíticas sanitarias, informes de inspecciones eléctricas y pruebas de protección contra incendios. También documentó todo lo relacionado con el control de operaciones (de accesos, circuitos eléctricos relacionados con la televisión o la telefonía) y actualizó el Plan de Autoprotección y registró los informes de salud pública y seguridad. A pesar de la subsanación y renovación de los elementos del estadio, la Comunidad de Madrid sigue adelante con el procedimiento de extinción de la concesión al Rayo Vallecano por “incumplimiento grave de sus obligaciones” y con la reforma integral del estadio. La afición quedó muy insatisfecha con las instalaciones el día del Trofeo de Vallecas y queda trabajo por hacer. La vuelta al estadio de Vallecas no son solo buenas noticias para los aficionados, sino para todos los comercios de la zona que el día en el que juega el Rayo prestan un servicio a todos aquellos aficionados que pasan por la zona. "El barrio se moviliza porque hay mucho negocio pequeño, y desde el carnicero, las tiendas de bebidas, o lo que sea, tiene que prepararse todo el mundo", cuenta Sara a MARCA, de El Salero de Ming. Un bar que está a escasos 200 metros del estadio y que sirve de lugar de reunión para todos los rayistas. La noticia de la suspensión de la actividad cayó como un jarro de agua fría para los comercios de la zona. Después de dos años en los que coincidió el Centenario, después la temporada europea y un verano de Mundial, el 28 de julio todo saltó por los aires. "Nos preocupó bastante. Estuvimos pensando a ver qué vamos a hacer porque el invierno siempre es más flojo que el verano", comenta Sara, socia de Ming. El Salero de Ming es uno de esos rincones donde los aficionados rayistas se reúnen y disfrutan del fútbol y de sus colores. "Cuando hay partido trabajamos fenomenal porque es gente del barrio muy maja. Se hace mucha comunidad, que también es algo que es muy agradable y se crea mucho ambiente de barrio", cuenta. El día del Trofeo de Vallecas volvió el fútbol al estadio, pero tan solo acudieron 4.462 aficionados y los comercios de la zona lo notaron. "Vino muy poca gente (al bar). Comentaron que las instalaciones siguen estando mal y que la gente no está contenta", afirma Sara. El fútbol vuelve al estadio de Vallecas y pese a que la situación no sea la mejor, los aficionados acudirán a la llamada de su equipo y el barrio entero se movilizará para disfrutar de la Franja.

articles.title: La Segunda recupera un partido entre filiales ocho años después: el último lo jugó Cucurella
articles.standfirst: El anterior a este Celta Fortuna-Real Sociedad B fue un Sevilla Atlético-Barça B en abril de 2018
articles.summary: El último precedente data de abril de 2018, cuando el Sevilla Atlético derrotó al Barça B
articles.body: La Segunda división española recupera este fin de semana un partido entre filiales. El Celta Fortuna recibirá en Balaídos (sábado, 21 horas) a la Real Sociedad B, con ambos equipos en horas bajas. Los vigueses sólo han rescatado un empate en las últimas cuatro jornadas y los donostiarras encadenan tres derrotas. Sus números son casi idénticos: 8 puntos, uno por encima de la zona que marca el descenso a Primera Federación, donde compartieron grupo en las temporadas 2023-2024 y 2024-2025. Para encontrar el anterior cruce entre filiales hay que retroceder hasta el 1 de abril de 2018. Ese día, el Sevilla Atlético de Tevenet derrotó 3-1 al Barça B, por entonces entrenado por Gerard López. En los azulgranas jugaban Cucurella, Aleñà, Abel Ruiz y Carles Pérez, entre otros. Ambos bajaron a Segunda B al final de esa campaña y no han vuelto a pisar la categoría de plata. La cantera es un gran orgullo para el Celta y la Real Sociedad, dos clubes inmersos en competición europea. Sus filiales tienen plantillas muy jóvenes que siguen nutriendo de futbolistas al primer equipo. Hugo Burcio y Andrés Antañón, en el conjunto gallego, y Luken Beitia y Álex Marchal, en el vasco, han jugado este curso con los mayores en Primera. Además, Ibai Aguirre, Lebarbier y Carrera han ido convocados por Matarazzo; y Ribes, por Claudio Giráldez. Los celestes presumen orgullosos de tener hasta 3 jugadores entre los 10 más jóvenes con minutos en LaLiga Hypermotion 2026-2027: David Sueiro (16 años), Vlad Silva (17) y Mateo Sobral (17).

articles.title: Tzolakis, un Adonis bajo los palos de la Premier esculpido por Mendilibar: "Valdrá 60, 70 u 80 millones"
articles.standfirst: El guardameta griego ha confirmado en el parón de selecciones las excelentes sensaciones transmitidas durante el inicio de temporada con el Hull City
articles.summary: El guardameta griego ha confirmado en el parón de selecciones las excelentes sensaciones transmitidas durante el inicio de temporada con el Hull City
articles.body: El entusiasmo generado alrededor de Grecia durante los últimos meses se ha confirmado durante esta Fecha FIFA. Los Tzolis, Karetsas, Kostoulas, Mouzakitis... y compañía levantan pasiones. Pero, bajo palos, Konstantinos Tzolakis (Chania, 2002) es el Adonis encargado de sostener el fuerte de una selección que aspira a regresar a un gran torneo de selecciones por primera vez desde el Mundial 2014. Desde que Nikolaos Papadopoulos le diese la oportunidad de debutar a nivel absoluto en junio de 2024, ha ido alternando el puesto con Odisseas Vlachodimos. Ivan Jovanovic, sin embargo, le ha entregado las llaves de la portería del combinado 'heleno'... siendo titular en las cuatro jornadas de la Nations League. Tiene gran parte de culpa, desde luego, de que Grecia marche colíder de su grupo y dependa de sí mismo para meterse en los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones: apenas ha encajado tres goles en cuatro partidos y ha dejado otras dos porterías a cero. Ambas, contra Alemania. Todo, después de realizar 15 intervenciones, ocho de ellas a remates desde dentro del área, que han servido para evitar 1.38 goles, según la estadística avanzada. Especialmente destacada, con hasta cinco paradas, fue su actuación en el primer partido contra Alemania que dejó 'secos' a los de Klopp. Tzolakis, sin embargo, trata de quitarse mérito. "Fue un trabajo de equipo. Todos defendimos durante mucho tiempo. En la primera parte no nos amenazaron tanto como en la segunda". El nivel mostrado durante el parón, confirmando sus excelentes dotes para blocar disparos, no es más que la continuación de lo que ya dejó claro durante este inicio de temporada en las filas de un Hull City que lo fichó el pasado verano por 23 millones. La segunda venta más cara en la historia de Olympiacos, sólo por detrás de Kostoulas. "Me siento preparado. Voy a darlo todo cada día para cumplir los objetivos", prometía. Durante su estancia en El Pireo, ganó cuatro Ligas, dos Copas, una Supercopa de Grecia... y la Conference League en 2024 contra la Fiorentina. Aquella noche, realizó cuatro paradas —todas desde dentro del área—, completó con éxito sus cuatro salidas fuera de la portería, despejo dos balones por alto y evitó 1.09 goles por parte del conjunto 'viola'. Especialmente meritoria fue una mano a Kouamé en el 69', con 0-0 en el marcador, para sacar el balón de la escuadra. "Desde que está con nosotros, Tzolakis ha sido un muy buen portero. Es el que siempre está ahí para protegernos, porque eso es lo que hace un portero: protege al equipo y para los goles de los rivales", dijo Mendi —jugó 99 partidos a sus órdenes— el pasado mes de enero. "Simplemente legendario. Lograste lo imposible. Gracias por todo", escribía el meta griego cuando se confirmó su salida de Olympiacos. El Hull City sabía que, para poder permanecer en Premier, necesitaban una garantía bajo palos... y Tzolakis está cumpliendo con creces. "Pensábamos en tres porteros de un nivel similar. Tzolakis era el más joven de ellos. Pero venía de Olympiacos, lo que era un gran 'plus' para mí", explicaba Sergej Jakirovic. "Allí vivía cada día bajo una presión enorme, así que jugar en el Hull es un gran alivio para él en ese sentido". Ocupando la portería del equipo que más pases permite al rival (145.9) y el que más pases permite en su tercio propio de campo (286), apenas ha encajado cuatro goles en cinco jornadas cuando le han generado seis. Es el cuarto guardameta con más paradas (17), el tercero desde dentro del área (13), segundo con más salidas exitosas (seis) y el primero con más porterías a cero (tres) junto a Verbruggen. "Cuando cambias de la Liga griega a la Premier, la mejor liga del mundo, es totalmente diferente. El nivel, la velocidad, todo. Primero tienes que pelear por ti mismo y luego mejorar tus habilidades", confesaba en una entrevista con la 'BBC'. "Me dijeron que, si hacía siete u ocho porterías a cero lograríamos la permanencia. Pusimos ese objetivo". En su última actuación, ante el Newcastle en St. James' Park, llegó a detenerle un penalti a Yoane Wissa... que no sirvió para evitar que el Hull sufriese la primera derrota de la temporada en su regreso a Premier. "Pronto valdrá 60, 70, 80 o quién sabe cuántos millones", apuntaba Jakirovic. Es, sin duda, el portero de moda en Inglaterra y, posiblemente, en el fútbol europeo.

articles.title: ¡Vuelve el fútbol (de clubes)!
articles.standfirst: Tras casi tres semanas de parón, las grandes ligas vuelven a arrancar
articles.summary: Tras casi tres semanas de parón, las grandes ligas vuelven a arrancar
articles.body: Las tres semanas que ha durado este primer ‘superparón’ de selecciones de la temporada 2026-27 parece que ha difuminado todo lo sucedido durante las primeras jornadas en las grandes ligas europeas. La vuelta, eso sí, viene con sorpresas. Y es que, a excepción del Barcelona en LaLiga, ninguna de las otras cuatro grandes ligas de Europa —Premier, Serie A, Bundesliga y Ligue 1— se encuentra liderada por sus vigentes campeones. Todo arrancará este viernes, en la previa de una nueva semana de Champions League, con partidos como el Borussia Dortmund - Werder Bremen en Alemania, el Al Nassr de Cristiano jugando en Arabia Saudí o el Lyon visitando el campo del Lens, vigente subcampeón galo. Además, fuera de los principales focos, equipos como el PSV, Sporting CP o Galatasaray también regresan a la acción. El Arsenal, que también había cosechado triunfos en la Community Shield, Champions League y Carabao Cup, vio frenado su impecable arranque de campaña en Premier sufriendo una dolorosa derrota —no perdían por una diferencia de tres goles en el campeonato doméstico desde mayo de 2023— frente al Brighton… cediendo así la primera plaza a un Manchester City que se marchó al parón con pleno (5/5) de victorias. Un escenario que entraba en pocas quinielas después de que Guardiola pusiese fin a una década prodigiosa en el Etihad. De hecho, sólo el propio Pellegrini (15-16) y propio Pep (16-17 y 23-24) lo habían logrado. “Es mucho mejor tener tres puntos más que menos. Pero sabemos que es bastante pronto. Durante el parón, podemos revisar lo que hemos hecho y lo que podemos mejorar”, exponía Enzo Maresca… consciente de que la primera prueba para reanudar la competición pasa por visitar Anfield en lo que se espera que sea un juicio público después de que su City haya sido declarado culpable de infringir 114 de los 115 cargos de los que le culpa la Premier. Ese Liverpool - Manchester City del domingo es el partido del fin de semana en Europa pero no el único gran duelo de la sexta jornada en Inglaterra: Arsenal - Leeds, Chelsea - Bournemouth o Manchester United - Tottenham tienen también su hueco destacado en la agenda de cualquier amanta del fútbol internacional. La igualdad en la parte alta del ‘Calcio’ es máxima. Roma e Inter firmaron las tablas en el Olímpico y la Lazio lo aprovechó para igualar sus 13 puntos en el liderato. Los ‘giallorossi’, eso sí, están a la cabeza por diferencia general de goles (+11). La ilusión está disparada en la Ciudad Eterna… y no es para menos tras haber cuajado el mejor arranque en Serie A de la última década. A la vuelta, eso sí, toca medirse al Como de Cesc en el Sinigaglia. “Debemos centrarnos en nuestros asuntos. Tenemos que tomar conciencia de que, en las condiciones adecuadas, podemos ser un equipo realmente peligroso”, expuso Gian Piero Gasperini tras el empate frente al Inter. Tiene los pies en el suelo… pero no renuncia a soñar con llevar a la Roma a ganar su primer 'Scudetto' desde 2001. “Nuestro plan era a tres años. No nos agradaría anticiparnos… pero somos conscientes de que el camino es largo”, decía en una entrevista con el ‘Corriere della Sera’. Ese Como - Roma, celebrado en la previa de la visita del Real Madrid al Olímpico, es el gran partido del fin de semana italiano... pero también destaca el Inter - Parma, el Nápoles - Frosinone, el Sassuolo - Milan o el Cagliari - Juventus. La Lazio de Gattuso, colíder en Italia, recibe al Monza en Roma. Que el Bayern Múnich no consiga enlazar su tercera ensaladera consecutiva bajo las órdenes de Vicent Kompany es algo que, parece, solo el Dortmund podría evitar. Y es que el inesperado empate contra el Schalke 04 —primer partido en Bundesliga sin marcar desde febrero de 2025 ante el Leverkusen— en la segunda jornada les tiene dos puntos por detrás de un Borussia Dortmund que ha sumado 12/12 puntos en las cuatro primeras fechas. La confianza sobre Niko Kovac continúa en entredicho. Pero lo cierto es que son números que, previamente, sólo se habían visto en tres ocasiones en el club… aunque sólo en una de ellas (01-02) se logró levantar el título. “Disfrutamos de esta posición en este momento, pero también sabemos que tenemos la responsabilidad de seguir trabajando duro para mantenerla el mayor tiempo posible”, dijo el técnico ‘borussen’ en la previa del partido ante el Werder Bremen. Es el Dortmund el que abre de nuevo la 'Bundes', hoy viernes, mientras que el Bayern tendrá que esperar al sábado para visitar el campo de un Augsburgo que se fue al parón como cuarto clasificado. El Leverkusen de Carles Martínez, mientras, 'vuelve' con visita al Mainz 05. El ajustado triunfo en ‘Le Classique’ permitió que el PSG esquivase el que hubiese sido su peor arranque de curso desde la 07-08. Están lejos, sin embargo, de los 13 puntos —cuatro victorias y un empate— cosechados por el Mónaco de Filipe Luís. Empezaron con un ajustado triunfo a domicilio contra Le Havre y, a partir de ahí, ganaron a Marsella, el propio PSG y Lens. El único ‘tropiezo’ llegó ante el Estrasburgo a domicilio. El técnico brasileño, ya con su licencia UEFA Pro en vigor, ha igualado así el mejor inicio de temporada en la historia del club… logrado, previamente, por Claudio Ranieri (13-14), Leonardo Jardim (16-17) y Adi Hütter (24-25). Sólo el actual técnico de Flamengo, eso sí, fue capaz de ‘destronar’ al PSG. “Estoy satisfecho, pero quiero mantener la humildad”, reconocía un Filipe Luís que, en ‘RMC Sport’, expuso que “no es realista pensar en el título”. El Monaco jugará en el Principado (ante el Toulouse) para sostener la primera plaza mientras que el PSG hará lo propio con el Le Mans en el Parque de los Príncipes.

articles.title: 'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'
articles.summary: Northern Ireland striker Simone Magill tells BBC Sport NI about balancing motherhood with her return to football and how her life has changed since giving bi...
articles.body:
"Football will always be a large part of my life but it's very much what I do, not who I am.

"Ultimately, I'm Skye's mum and, to me, that's the most important thing."

Through her 16-year footballing career, Simone Magill has been something of a trailblazer in Northern Ireland.

From a senior debut at the age of 15, helping the country to a major tournament debut and becoming captain, she has been there and seen it all.

But after giving birth to her first child, Skye, in May, her focus is paving the way off the pitch, as well as on it.

"I think we get labelled as athletes, and that is our complete entire identity," Birmingham City striker Magill told BBC Sport.

"Obviously there's been a massive shift now. I'm a mum first and foremost and that is the highest title that I will ever have.

"Family is so important. It's my priority, and it's so nice for me to have that greater purpose now.

"It's hard and it can be overwhelming, but it's the greatest joy that I've ever experienced in my life."

Magill is speaking at the Northern Ireland camp in the lead up to Friday's World Cup play-off with Portugal.

While she is stepping up her training four months on from giving birth, the first round of play-offs have come too soon.

However, after conversations with manager Michael McArdle, who has spoken about the importance of family , the 31-year-old is in camp to train with the squad.

More importantly, Skye and her husband, Mark, are with her for the duration.

It is a glimpse into what the future will look like when Magill is back playing for Northern Ireland.

"It's so different, but it's so special. I'm really enjoying being back in, and I think I find it weirder having my husband here than having Skye," she said.

"It's just amazing that I'm able to do this and the support that I've been given to allow me to do this has made things so much easier."

After nearly a year away from the squad, from when she announced her pregnancy last November, she says the support that the Irish FA and her Northern Ireland team-mates have provided has meant "I don't need to worry about anything".

Skye and Mark have become fully integrated in the camp and join the team for meals and in downtime.

Then, when it comes to on-pitch matters and meetings, Mark is able to look after Skye and Magill can focus on the football side of things.

"Mark has his daddy-daughter days with her while I'm on the training pitch.

"Then when I'm here with the girls in and around the hotel and free times, we're all here mingling with Skye.

"She's now got 23 aunties who are all very hands-on."

Before camp, Magill admits there was a bit of apprehension about how integrating back into the group with Skye may look, but "I feel a sense of obligation to pave the way".

While she is not the first Northern Ireland player to have a child and return to playing - experienced defender Sarah McFadden gave birth to her second child in 2024 - Magill is the first to have the family integrated into the camp.

"So it's the unknown of what things are going to look like," she said.

"It's relatively new in the game and I suppose I'm one of the first people certainly here and at club as well to do this.

"There are going to be certain things that we might need a little bit more support with, but we don't know that until we go through each phase and we're navigating that all collaboratively."

'Can I still play if I can't bring her?'

Magill feels that having Skye with the group is "lovely for the mood" and "gets everyone involved" as the new arrival is the most popular member of the camp.

She added that having Skye and Mark in camp has been "game-changing", and pointed to how a new mother in a more traditional job would have a year off, while her career means she is looking to get back on the pitch as quick as possible.

"If I didn't have that support then it almost questions, 'can I still play football if I can't bring her?'

"But it means that I can fully focus on being a footballer, but equally put everything into still being a mum at the same time."

While Skye has yet to be given a club team to support - Magill has played for Everton and Aston Villa before joining Birmingham and Mark supports Manchester United - there is no debate surrounding her international allegiance.

Despite Mark being from England, Skye has already been decked out in a mini-Northern Ireland kit.

"It's so important for me that she can come back to Northern Ireland often and just be surrounded by Northern Irish accents, to show her where I've come from and my roots. It's really special."

Magill said that she and Mark, who got married in 2021 after meeting at university, had always wanted to start a family and "we almost had to remove football from that decision".

While she stopped playing matches when she found out she was expecting, she was still active in training and the gym right up to a few weeks before Skye was born.

Just four weeks after her arrival, Magill was back doing gym work and she was back on the pitch after 13 weeks.

Now fully training again, she hopes to be back playing matches later in the autumn.

"It's funny because when I announced my pregnancy, I think the natural assumption from a lot of people in the scope of wider things thought that that was probably going to be the end of my football career.

"But I was like, 'well, no, absolutely not'.

"I very much wanted to be a voice and showcase that you can be a mum and a footballer, and those things can both co-exist."

Magill has spent longer away from playing matches than when she sustained an ACL injury at Euro 2022, but the stresses of rehab are absent.

For Magill, Skye has given her a new drive and purpose. Only five games away from a century of international caps, she dreams of walking out onto the pitch with her in her arms.

"Skye will not necessarily remember any of this, but I will.

"When she's older she can look back and see the hard work that I put in to come back and play, and it was all for her.

"All throughout my pregnancy I was almost manifesting that moment that when I make my return and being able to carry her out onto the pitch, I think, you know, that's what's driving me."

Magill said that McFadden was a role model for her when it came to balancing family and football, and now she wants to inspire other players to take the same step.

"We have a lot of younger members in the squad now and hopefully it is a very normal thing for them to see that this can be done.

"You know that there's a player playing for the team that has a child and she's able to bring the child in.

"That's very important to be normalised now in our sport and I'm just so thankful that the support systems are in place to allow me to do this.

"I've always wanted to inspire people on the pitch, but hopefully this is something I've done off the pitch that could also inspire future generations to show that it's possible."
authors: Andy Gray - BBC Sport NI Journalist

articles.title: La promesa de Mou al Bernabéu: "Si un jugador del Madrid no se comporta como jugador del Madrid no le vais a ver ni en el banquillo"
articles.standfirst: El portugués asegura que no le temblará la mano si un jugador no cumple dentro o fuera del campo
articles.summary: El portugués asegura que no le temblará la mano si un jugador no cumple dentro o fuera del campo
articles.body: josé Mourinho dejó claro en su rueda de prensa que no le temblará la mano si un jugador no cumple con sus obligaciones dentro o fuera del campo. Se llame como se llame. Así de claro lo afirmó cuando le preguntaron por Kylian Mbappé, al que defendió a capa y espada diciendo que todo el ruido que se ha montado a su alrededor es "ridículo". Para Mou, Mbappé ha cumplido a rajatabla con todo lo que le ha pedido el club y dejó claro que si algún jugador no se comporta como se debe comportar un jugador del Madrid, será castigado. Así fue la promesa de Mourinho a los aficionados del Real Madrid: "Yo prometo que si un jugador del Madrid no se comporta como jugador del Real Madrid y falla como jugador del Real Madrid, no cumple con sus obligaciones como jugador o como ciudadano, no van a ver aese jugador en banquillo. No van a poder pitarlo. Va a estar en casa. No le doy la oportunidad de sentarse en el banquillo. Y Mbappé va a jugar. Ni en el banquillo estará. Estoy seguro de que no ha fallado con sus obligaciones con el Real Madrid". Para Mou, el caso Mbappé no existe y lo explica así: "Mbappé ha estado aquí, se hizo el diagnóstico y se fue para una segunda opinión porque tiene algo en la rodilla que no se puede olvidar. Durante la recuperación, que vosotros no tenéis que saber al detalle, y luego entramos en el campo de la búsqueda por problemas. Primero era la discoteca que no era discoteca... era una discoteca transformada para la moda en París para un evento privado. Después la bicicleta en Suiza, en el que había un par de bicicletas para ir al spa, a las zonas comunes y de tranquilidad absoluta. Y llegamos a casos menores, como el pobre de Huijsen, que estaba parado en la casa de Pitarch y estaba mandando un mensaje y parecía casi un criminal...".

articles.title: Fidalgo regresa tras sus partidos con México y Pellegrini tendrá disponible a casi toda su plantilla ante Osasuna
articles.standfirst: Sólo Junior, lesionado, y Ruibal, en fase de puesta a punto, son baja frente a los rojillos
articles.summary: Sólo Junior, lesionado, y Ruibal, en fase de puesta a punto, son baja frente a los rojillos
articles.body: Álvaro Fidalgo ha sido la principal novedad en la penúltima sesión de entrenamiento del Betis esta semana, en la que el conjunto verdiblanco ha seguido con su preparación del partido de la octava jornada de Liga que disputará el domingo en La Cartuja frente a Osasuna. El centrocampista asturiano, tras sus partidos con México, ha sido el último de los internacionales en sumarse al grupo y estará disponible para el primer compromiso de su equipo tras la larga fecha FIFA de finales de septiembre y principios de octubre. Con la vuelta de Fidalgo, Pellegrini tiene ya disponible a la práctica totalidad de su plantilla. Sólo Junior Firpo, que estará unas tres semanas de baja por una lesión muscular, está estos días en la enfermería verdiblanca. Mientras que Aitor Ruibal, de baja desde mayo por una cirugía del menisco externo, sigue avanzando en su trabajo con el grupo, aunque todavía necesitará algunas sesiones de entrenamiento más antes de estar disponible para regresar a la competición. Los verdiblancos reciben al conjunto rojillo con la intención de prolongar su impecable racha de resultados en casa, donde cuentan por victoria todos sus encuentros en lo que va de temporada. Con solo dos bajas confirmadas, Diego Llorente y Bartra recuperados y todos los internacionales ya de vuelta, Pellegrini tendrá que realizar algún descarte y decidir si incorpora a la lista al canterano Carlos de Roa, lateral zurdo del filial que ha trabajado estos días con el grupo. El Ingeniero ofrecerá este mediodía su rueda de prensa oficial previa al partido, aunque la convocatoria probablemente no la haga pública hasta después del entrenamiento de mañana.

articles.title: What could Rangers' 2012 case tell us about Man City's uncertain future?
articles.summary: From sanctions and stripped titles to starting from scratch, BBC Scotland explains how potential consequences for Manchester City compare with the financial collapse of Rangers in 2012.
articles.body:
In the wake of Manchester City 's unprecedented guilty verdict, the scramble to source similar situations to help shed light on what could come next continues.

But finding a direct comparison has been a struggle because of that very word: unprecedented.

Some have attempted to draw parallels with the demise of Rangers in 2012 as an ominous, dark cloud of uncertainty hangs over the Premier League leaders.

From sanctions and stripped titles to starting from scratch, BBC Scotland explains how potential consequences for City compare with the financial collapse of the Ibrox club and which led to a giant of the British game being dumped at the bottom of the Scottish football ladder.

Clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal

Rangers boss McInnes 'not a fan' of extended break

What Guardiola said about Man City charges

It's a long story that, at this stage, doesn't really compare a whole lot to City's.

Rangers' case ultimately became an insolvency event after the club racked up huge tax liabilities. The Employee Benefit Trust (EBT) scheme was a major part of that.

Under former owner Sir David Murray, Rangers paid money into EBTs for employees - including players, managers and directors - for about a decade at the turn of the millennium.

In total, more than £47m came out of the trusts to more than 80 individuals. HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) argued the payments should have been taxed as earnings and therefore that Rangers owed substantial sums.

After lengthy court and tribunal proceedings, the Supreme Court definitively ruled in favour of HMRC in its fight with Rangers over the use of EBTs. That came five years after the old company's liquidation.

City, meanwhile, have been found to have arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise more than £830m of funding, according to the Premier League.

The Manchester club have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the league's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. City have appealed against the verdict and deny any wrongdoing.

Sanctions, stripped titles and re-entering league system

With the threat of serious sanctions hanging over City, we wait to find out what comes next.

In Rangers' case, entering administration in February of the 2011-12 season meant a 10-point deduction was triggered. They finished the campaign in second, 20 points behind champions Celtic.

No further penalties were applied, with liquidation ensuing in June 2012.

Rangers were also never stripped of any honours they won during the years they used EBTs, which were ruled to have not gained them "any unfair competitive advantage".

Where things get a bit fiddly, confusing and the source of debate among fans, is the distinction between Rangers the club and Rangers the company.

Following the liquidation, the football assets - including Ibrox, the training ground, name and brand - were acquired by a new company led by Charles Green.

Despite the team continuing to play at Ibrox with the same colours and badge, jibes about Rangers not being the same club are heard from opposing fans at every match.

After Green bought the assets, a vote took place to decide whether Rangers could remain in the top tier. Ten of the 12 top-flight clubs voted against the application, with Kilmarnock abstaining and Rangers voting in favour.

Rangers then had to apply to play in the lower leagues, which at the time were governed by the Scottish Football League, a body separate from the top flight, then called the Scottish Premier League.

This shares similarities with the current set-up in England, with the Premier League separate from the English Football League, which governs the Championship, League One and League Two.

Premier League expulsion has been hypothetically discussed as a potential sanction for City. That could mean they then have to apply to be accepted into the EFL, just as Rangers did with the old SFL.

The Scottish FA recommended Rangers enter the second tier, but that was rejected by the majority of SFL clubs, with 25 of the 30 voting for Rangers to enter the fourth tier instead.

TV deals, 'heartbreaking' ordeals and a ball on a hedge

There were fears that without Rangers in the top flight, TV deals would be under threat without Old Firm derbies, putting clubs at financial risk.

Neil Doncaster, the league's chief executive, initially described the reduction in broadcast income as "slight" but acknowledged "there will be money coming out the game as a result of Rangers not being in the top flight".

So what would the loss of Manchester derbies do to the Premier League's?

Then manager Ally McCoist continued in his post following Rangers' demotion and led the team through the fourth and third tiers with relative ease.

The Ibrox icon recently described the 2012 ordeal as an "absolutely horrendous" situation because of the job losses that occurred.

"You're not talking about your centre-forward or centre-back," he said on Talksport. "I had one of the older lads in tears, not a player, just someone who had a wee job, because he was losing his job. It was heartbreaking."

On the pitch, however, McCoist recalled a bizarre but "unbelievable" journey through the lower leagues, hailing the commitment of the fanbase.

"I'll never forget one of the opening games," he added. "We played Brechin and the game got delayed because the ball got stuck on the top of a hedge."

The former striker also said he was dragged off the team bus by the Peterhead chairman to speak to fans in a marquee and did the half-time draw in a social club before his side faced Annan Athletic.

'The players won't stay - you're starting from scratch'

McCoist left midway through Rangers' first Championship season, which ended with them being denied a third straight promotion when they were beaten 6-1 on aggregate by Motherwell in the play-off final.

Mark Warburton arrived in the summer of 2015 and was the man to guide Rangers back to the Premiership.

Just one league title, delivered under Steven Gerrard in 2020-21, has come in the following decade.

Attempting to translate how that would look for City is a challenge given the difference in financial disparity between England and Scotland.

Even in the fourth tier, the budget Rangers were operating with still allowed them to attract some of the Premiership's top talent. That continued throughout their rise through the divisions.

It would be difficult to picture City enticing Premier League players to join them in the event of a severe demotion. And that is before you consider their squad being ripped apart.

Due to the nature of Rangers' plight, they lost a host of integral players without being able to recoup a penny.

The likes of Steven Davis, Steven Naismith and Allan McGregor were among those to lodge objections to a transfer to the 'newco'.

For City, they would at least be able to bring in cash for departing stars, permitting any potential contract clauses.

City fan Matt Mellor joked he "can't wait to see Erling Haaland bag a hat-trick against Grimsby" in League Two next season. McCoist isn't convinced.

"When you go down there, you're effectively starting from scratch, because the players won't stay," the Rangers great said.

"If you're talking about Manchester City , you're starting again. You're officially starting again."

articles.title: Andoni Iraola: Five key issues facing Liverpool boss ahead of Man City showdown
articles.summary: Liverpool take on Man City at Anfield on Super Sunday as new head coach Andoni Iraola looks to maintain his unbeaten start to his Reds reign; Watch Liverpool vs Man City live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm.
articles.body:
The recent international break has not been kind to Iraola, with key men Alexander Isak [thigh], Cody Gakpo [ankle] and Jeremy Jacquet [hamstring] having all returned early to the AXA Training Centre with injury.

The France defender will be available, though, to face City, Iraola has since confirmed in his pre-match press conference, although there was less good news about his attacking duo.

"Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo will not play the game. They are not ready. They both don't look like long-term," said the Reds boss, meaning an untimely change of personnel will be required in the forward line.

The pair's absence is a massive blow for Iraola, especially given the understanding Isak and Gakpo have developed so far, while the Swede's thigh injury also leaves a huge hole to fill in the No 9 role after his impressive start to the campaign that has seen him score four times in the Premier League already.

All of which could mean Lewis Koumas, 21, deputising for Isak, with Hugo Ekitike still months away from recovering from his ruptured Achilles.

Will players be able to cope with 'demanding' schedule?

Liverpool now face a tricky run of seven games in three different competitions over the course of the next three weeks that will test both the players' fitness levels, as well as Iraola's own ability to rotate and manage their workloads.

That fixture list includes a daunting trip to take on in-form Brentford, followed by home games with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion and champions Arsenal in the league, either side of Chelsea visiting Anfield in the League Cup.

Iraola has so far only had to prepare for one league game after a Champions League encounter and it is revealing it was the underwhelming goalless home draw against winless Fulham that came just three days on from an energy-sapping win over Atletico Madrid.

How the Basque navigates this period - and remember he never had to contend with such a packed schedule while at Bournemouth - could be key to how the his side fare during this run, something the Reds boss is all too well aware of.

"We still have to get ready because the schedule that we have now, it's very difficult," he said. "We are playing against top-four teams and then in between Champions League and then in between Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and everything in two, three days.

"So we have to get ready because this next month, after this break, it's going be very demanding for us."

The elephant in Liverpool's room continues to be £116m signing Florian Wirtz and even more so after the German's latest anonymous display at Bournemouth just prior to the international break.

"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Jamie Carragher of Wirtz's performance at the Vitality on the Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.

"I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break. By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something!"

With injuries to Gakpo and Isak, though, Iraola will now need his two other £100m attackers - Wirtz and Bradley Barcola - to shine in order to get a result against City, with the Reds boss no doubt hoping Jurgen Klopp's star dust may have rubbed off on his compatriot during the recent international break.

Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam, however, is adamant Iraola will get the best out of the playmaker.

"Liverpool beat off Bayern Munich and Man City to sign Wirtz, he was probably one of the most coveted No 10s in world football at the time and Liverpool have attracted him," McAdam said on the latest Sky Sports Premier League podcast.

"So he does not become a bad No 10 overnight, I just think there are some basics there that will need to be sorted - the physicality of the Premier League, the ability to make decisions far quicker than he has ever had to do and what is his best role within that Liverpool side?

"I'm convinced Iraola will have everything within what they do to find the best in him and that is what he has done historically, he has always found the right role for players."

Can the right balance be found in midfield?

Iraola favours a two-man midfield to both screen the back four, as well as break up opposition attacks while starting their own counters, but this very much remains a work in progress.

Interestingly, it is Ryan Gravenberch - such a key figure under previous head coach Arne Slot - who has been the one to miss out, with the Reds boss favouring a partnership of Alexis Mac Allister, revitalised after a slump last season, and Dominik Szoboszlai as his twin No 6s.

And having conceded twice in each of their opening two Premier League games at Newcastle United and home to Nottingham Forest, Liverpool have since kept three straight clean sheets for the first time since the start of their 2024/25 title-winning campaign as the Basque looks to find the right balance in front of the defence.

"He [Iraola] is still trying to strive for that ideal balance in that Liverpool midfield at times," SSN reporter Vinny O'Connor said on the Sky Sports Premier League podcast.

"But with those three clean sheets in the Premier League in the last three games, we are seeing a team that defends the box a lot better and when they get the ball, they get it forward a lot quicker and creating chances as well, which bodes well for the future."

One clear indicator Liverpool's players are buying into the new manager's way of playing is they top the Premier League for most sprints [636] after the opening five games, although conversely they are also bottom when it comes to distance covered [551.36km - but that is often just a reflection of how much possession a team has enjoyed].

Get the press right and as O'Connor predicts: "I do not think we are too far away from seeing that more regular high-octane football under him."

Can Iraola get statement Anfield win to kick-start Reds reign?

On the one hand, Iraola heads into Sunday's game having made an unbeaten start to life as Liverpool head coach, making the 44-year-old the first manager not to lose any of his first five league games in charge of Liverpool since Joe Fagan all the way back in September 1983.

However, those opening five top-flight contests have been favourable to the Basque and as we noted earlier, things now start getting harder - starting with the visit of the league leaders this Sunday - meaning we will be able to make a better judgement about his Reds start come November.

One anomaly Iraola will be desperate to correct against City this weekend, however, is the lack of a home league win so far under his tenure - in fact, you have to go all the way back to April 26 against Crystal Palace, five games ago, for their last victory at Anfield.

The new man has masterminded impressive home wins against Atletico Madrid and Tottenham Hotspur in the Champions League and League Cup respectively so far this campaign, but recording a statement Premier League win would be transformative for him.

"That big win in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid is a massive plus because not only does that show that they can win games, but they can do it against the big teams, the big hitters, those sides that are going to challenge them," McAdam said.

However, as Liverpool podcaster and writer Dan Morgan also pointed out: "From a Liverpool supporter, I think there is still that anticipation of, 'OK, when is the big moment going to arrive?' And there's a big opportunity on Sunday…"

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Enzo Maresca says 'titles absolutely not tainted'
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club's titles are "absolutely not" tainted after they were found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
articles.body:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club's titles are "absolutely not" tainted after they were found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.

Maresca reiterated his faith in the club's owners and belief that they will win their appeal against the verdict during a news conference on Friday dominated by questions on the matter.

The Italian, notably relaxed as he offered his responses, rejected the suggestion City's titles have been tainted by the ruling, as he knows "exactly the effort that the club put in to achieve" them.

An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The club have appealed against the verdict and claimed in a statement the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

Preparing to play their first match since that verdict was announced, away to rivals Liverpool on Sunday, Maresca said in an in-house interview on Thursday the "feeling is fantastic" among his players and they are not affected by "the noise" surrounding the club.

He added on Friday: "The reason I joined this club is that I completely trust, 100%, the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, all the organisation. So I don't have doubt about that.

"I spoke with the club for sure. We all trust, and probably the right moment to speak about that is when we are going to win this appeal."

He added: "For me, the players - we can control just the pitch side, the football side. So we are focused on that. This is what we can do and what we can control."

Appointed as Pep Guardiola's successor in June, Maresca is in his third spell at the club following time spent with the academy and as Guardiola's assistant coach - including during the Treble-winning 2022-23 campaign.

The 46-year-old has won each of his first five Premier League games in charge of City, and could become the fourth manager to win his first six of a spell in charge of a club in the competition at Liverpool on Sunday.

The announcement of the verdict reached by an independent panel, which found City guilty of 'sham' contracts and misleading accounts as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m, means Maresca's side will expect to receive an even more hostile reception than usual at Anfield.

Asked if he had any concerns over the atmosphere during the match, Maresca said: "It will be a tough game, for sure. We need to be ready, the focus needs to be about the game, but we know the environment at Anfield.

"It probably will be worse because of the situation but, again, it will be our duty to do our best and try to win the game.

"The reason I decide to become manager is for this type of game."

Maresca thanked one journalist who asked a question not related to the verdict, confirming talisman Erling Haaland is "ready" to play against Liverpool after recovering from his efforts for Norway during the international break in Marbella.

Maresca will be demanding a siege mentality from Man City - Pulis

From doomscrolling to defiance - how do Man City fans feel?

What reception awaits Man City at Anfield?

Maresca would not confirm whether he has read the independent commission's findings.

The former Leicester City and Chelsea boss said the charges against the club were not discussed during his conversations about taking the job in the summer.

And he insisted he would "100%" have still accepted the role had the findings been published before an agreement was reached.

"We didn't speak about that because I don't think it was a problem for the club at the time and I think they are are thinking in an honest way," Maresca said.

"I think they are convinced that in the end we are going to win the appeal."

Earlier on Friday, Bayern Munich manager and former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany said: "I played 11 years for the club and I've loved all the years I've played for the club. Everything we've achieved and done on the pitch I'm really proud of.

"Everything else, as a player you're not a part of that. Right now, as a coach of Bayern Munich, I'm not too occupied with that topic."

'Uncertainty not good for anyone' - Premier League bosses have their say

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, who spent time as assistant to Guardiola at Manchester City prior to taking charge of the Gunners, echoed Maresca's faith in his former club's leadership team.

"[The] titles absolutely [are] not tainted. I trust the club now, in the future, always. I completely trust the club," said the Spaniard.

"I will respect the process. It is still an ongoing process that is not resolved because it has been appealed."

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola and Chelsea 's Xabi Alonso both stressed the need for patience following City's appeal.

"I think uncertainty is not good for anyone and anyone involved, but the process is ongoing and we have to patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end," Iraola said.

Alonso added: "We need to wait for the final sanctions from the panel. I think they are independent enough to assess all the situations.

"We have to be patient for sure. It is out of our hands, we have to respect the independence of the panel and see what happens."

Everton were deducted 10 points in November 2023 - in a punishment later reduced to six on appeal - and then docked two points in April 2024 in separate cases for breaches of profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

"I wasn't here when it was difficult for Everton , when things were bad," said Toffees boss David Moyes.

"Looking at it now from where I am sitting, it looks terrible that we have been docked points and pay some fines and not that long ago.

"There's other things that have been going on - nearly 10 years ago - that have not been dealt with. I find that really difficult.

"I hope it's not just Everton who are getting picked on here."

Nottingham Forest were another club punished previously for breaching PSR rules, with the City Ground side docked four points in March 2024.

"There is no final verdict right now. That's why I don't see any point to comment on Man City because I can't," said Forest boss Oliver Glasner.

"But let's say in general, if somebody cheats he needs to get punished. If not, then not. And of course, we all hope for the integrity of the game, for the integrity of the Premier League, that the final word is spoken soon.

"But we also know, I think there are thousands of pages to read. I read a book every night, and it takes quite long to read thousands of pages and also then find the final verdict, so it takes a little bit of time. We have to be patient, but yes, it should be soon."

articles.body: Rubén de la Barrera afronta la visita a Mallorca con ocho bajas seguras y la duda de Recoba, un escenario que le obliga a seguir buscando alternativas para confeccionar un once competitivo en un partido de máxima importancia. Jesé, Sandro, Marvin, Clemente, Sergio Ruiz, Viti, Cedeño y Ale García no estarán, mientras que el técnico sí confirmó que "Opoku está disponible de cara al domingo". Las ausencias condicionan especialmente la defensa, donde De la Barrera maneja distintas opciones para cubrir los laterales: "Álex puede ayudar en el lateral derecho, y a Valentín lo veo preparado para jugar por la derecha o izquierda", aunque la continuidad de Pezzolesi en el costado derecho parece limitar las alternativas. Otra de las opciones es el filial Adrián, al que ve preparado para ser titular. El entrenador ha reconocido la dimensión del problema: "Las lesiones musculares representan prácticamente nada del parte de bajas. Han sido frutos de las circunstancias, algunas arrastradas del pasado año", explicó. De la Barrera tampoco escondió su preocupación por una situación que condiciona la preparación de cada encuentro: "Llevo mucho tiempo en esto y el número de bajas es muy bestia. Es un factor que limita a todos". Los malos resultados del equipo pueden acelerar el futuro del entrenador, y una derrota en Mallorca, todavía más. De la Barrera, sin embargo, evitó alimentar las especulaciones: "No hemos hablado nada. Me ocupa y me preocupa el partido del domingo". Preguntado por si sería injusto un despido, teniendo en cuenta la plaga de bajas que ha sufrido el equipo durante el curso, tampoco quiso entrar a valorar esa posibilidad: "En el fútbol no hay justicias o injusticias". El resultado del domingo podría marcar su futuro, aunque el técnico prefiere aparcar cualquier debate.

articles.title: Man City charges: Enzo Maresca says owners 'convinced' club will win appeal against guilty verdict as he 'trusts' hierarchy
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca was speaking for the first time since Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules; Man City face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, live on Sky Sports with kick-off at 4.30pm
articles.body:
Speaking at his first press conference since the verdict was announced, Maresca insisted he "100 per cent completely trusts" the club's hierarchy, making him believe "we're going to win the appeal".

In his 15-minute press conference ahead of Sunday's game at Liverpool, live on Sky Sports , the Italian also said:

Man City's achievements are "absolutely not" tainted

"The right time to speak is when we win the appeal"

Admitted he had not read the findings of the commission

Believes everyone is on "the same page" at the club

Backs his team to handle Sunday's "even worse" Anfield environment and called for his players to "stick together"

The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Man City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

Last Friday, City confirmed their appeal because they are "innocent" and described the judgement against them as "opinion" and claimed it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

Maresca, who was assistant to Pep Guardiola in the 2022/23 treble-winning season, replaced the Spaniard as head coach this summer.

Asked if he would still have joined the club had the verdict been released earlier, he replied: "I know the organisation from years ago. I know how serious they are. I know they do the right things."

Questioned on whether the charges issue was raised during talks, he responded: "No, we didn't speak about that. I didn't think that was a problem for the club at that time. Also, because they are thinking in an honest way.

"I think they are convinced that in the end we will win the appeal."

Earlier he said: "The reason why I joined this club is I completely trust 100 per cent, the owner, the sporting director, the CEO - all the organisation. I have no doubt about that.

"I spoke with the club for sure. Probably the right moment to speak about that is when we're going to win this appeal."

Maresca says City's achievements not tainted

Asked whether the trophies won during the period in question were tainted, Maresca replied: "Absolutely not. I know the effort from the players, the club and the manager at the time, Pep (Guardiola), so I don't have any doubt about that.

He added: "There is not another club in the world where I would like to be."

Maresca admitted he had not read the findings of the commission.

"Again, I trust the club. I promise you my focus is just about football so I'm not thinking about different things because, first of all, I don't understand about many things," he said ahead of Sunday's trip to Anfield.

"For me, for the players, we can control just the football side. We are focused on that and that is what we can control, we can't control anything different.

"We just try to manage the noise. We understand the seriousness of the situation, the noise. We just need to manage that. We have to go to Anfield and win the game."

"I think it was a media masterclass from Enzo Maresca about how to deal with tough questions when you are in the middle of a media storm.

"Man City will be delighted with the way he handled that. It is not good news for journalists because we didn't really get a moment.

"There are not going to be big headlines that you will say. What I thought was interesting was his body language.

"City will be really happy about that. He was relaxed; at the end of it, he was smiling and joking. He didn't look like someone who was cornered.

"He didn't look like somebody under pressure. He kept to the script.

"He gave very little away and just kept saying that he trusts the owners and we have to wait for the appeal. I can only focus on the pitch; we can only control the controllables.

"He was also asked the question about whether it should it be the chairman or CEO doing this press conference, instead of you [Maresca], but again, he didn't give anything away."

The view from inside the press conference...

Sky Sports News reporter Ben Ransom from the press conference:

"My dealings with Enzo Maresca don't go back that long in the sense that he only joined as the manager in the summer. I've obviously sat here and done press conferences with him every week since he joined, and he has always presented himself like that: relaxed and calm.

"He must have also, at the back of his mind, known that at some point the independent commission were going to release their findings.

"Well, as far as Maresca is concerned today, he reiterated the statement and that the idea of the club are innocent. That's certainly what they have said all along and because of that appeal, I suppose, it made it a bit easier for him in the sense that he can defend the club on that basis.

"He held himself really well, and he kept his composure all the way through.

"How many different ways can a room full of journalists ask essentially the same question to try and get some sort of an emotional reaction out of him? We found out in 15 minutes, everyone had a little try, different ways into that conversation, but he handled it very well, and there wasn't quite the same emotion that we saw, for example, when Pep Guardiola sat down and responded very bullishly when the charges were initially announced in February 2023.

"Maresca was here at the club at that point. Remember, he was Pep's assistant at the time, so it was interesting to just get a sense of the fact that perhaps he's been, in a way, preparing ever since that time, looking at how Pep dealt with it, certainly in-house as well and the communications and the way he spoke to both the media and then the players inside and outside the building.

"In that sense, we shouldn't be surprised, but a few in the room probably will be that he managed to stick to the script as he did all the way through that and essentially will be pretty happy when he watches it back."

'Maresca more open on guilty verdict than expected'

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter from the press conference:

"Enzo Maresca presented an unflappable figure during 15 minutes of questioning on the Premier League's findings. He didn't trip once.

"His calm and considered responses were impressive given the room was packed with national journalists from almost every outlet. I counted 14 cameras. That is not usual.

"And he was more open than I expected him to be, referring back his focus on the football, but also standing firm on his stance that he trusts the club '100 per cent'.

"I do think he's got a bit of a 'get out of jail' card while Manchester City remain top of the league. He can legitimately refer back to that as a job well done - wins always quieten scrutiny.

"The difficult part will be if results turn at any point. Maresca will be asked if his squad are distracted, or have been impacted by what he describes as 'just noise'.

"No doubt that so-called noise will be deafening at Anfield. He's passed this first test. The next one comes this weekend."

How will City's perfect start be affected by verdict?

"Anfield is famous for its atmosphere, but the mood awaiting Manchester City on Sunday will be unique. What a venue for City's first game since an independent commission judged they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018. Seismic.

"City are appealing, of course, but the Liverpool crowd will deliver their own verdict and expect it to be vociferous. On the pitch, for what that is worth, Enzo Maresca's City side are defending a perfect record of five wins from five and are currently top of the table.

"Andoni Iraola is also unbeaten since taking over at Liverpool but with three draws from their opening five games, this feels like the first big test of his reign - and his team's own title credentials. Whatever happens, all eyes will be on an Anfield clash to remember."

articles.title: El Everton, en venta
articles.standfirst: El grupo Friedkin, dueño del club de Merseyside, está explorando nuevas vías de inversión
articles.summary: El grupo Friedkin, dueño del club de Merseyside, está explorando nuevas vías de inversión
articles.body: Los despachos de los clubes de la Premier siguen echando humo, y lamentablemente, el motivo nada tiene que ver con la adquisición de nuevos y pujantes jugadores para el campeonato doméstico, como está siendo habitual en los últimos cursos. El Everton anunció este viernes que The Friedkin Group, propietario del club desde diciembre de 2024, está estudiando nuevas fórmulas de inversión que incluyen la posible venta de una participación mayoritaria de la entidad. La noticia llega menos de dos años después de que el conglomerado estadounidense completara la compra del club de Liverpool, una operación que puso fin a la etapa de Farhad Moshiri y que entonces fue presentada como el inicio de un proyecto estable y a largo plazo. En el comunicado, los propietarios justifican su decisión recordando el contexto en el que desembarcaron en Goodison Park. "Cuando TFG se convirtió en custodio del Everton, el club afrontaba una importante incertidumbre financiera y desafíos tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego". El grupo subraya que su prioridad fue aportar estabilidad económica, inversión y apoyo para garantizar el futuro de la institución, además de ayudar a culminar el nuevo estadio del club. Ahora consideran que esa base ya está consolidada. "Con esos cimientos ya asegurados, ha llegado el momento de considerar el próximo capítulo para el Everton". Pese a abrir la puerta a un cambio de propiedad, los Friedkin aseguran que serán selectivos en el proceso. "Solo estudiaremos propuestas de partes que creamos firmemente que serán los administradores adecuados para llevar al club hacia adelante y construir sobre el impulso ya generado". Desde la entidad insisten además en que el apoyo al equipo no se verá afectado mientras duren las conversaciones con posibles inversores y aseguran que seguirán respaldando al club "en todo lo necesario para lograr el éxito sobre el terreno de juego". La decisión vuelve a sembrar incertidumbre alrededor de uno de los históricos del fútbol inglés, justo cuando el equipo dirigido por David Moyes trata de consolidar su proyecto deportivo tras años marcados por problemas. El Grupo Friedkin está explorando nuevas opciones de inversión para el Everton Football Club, incluida la posible venta de una participación mayoritaria. Cuando TFG se hizo cargo del Everton, el club se enfrentó a una importante incertidumbre financiera y a desafíos tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego. La prioridad inmediata fue brindar la estabilidad, la inversión y el apoyo necesarios para asegurar el futuro del club, incluyendo la finalización del tan esperado estadio para sus merecidos seguidores. Ahora que esta base está bien establecida, es el momento idóneo para considerar el próximo capítulo del Everton. Solo consideraremos el interés de aquellas partes que, a nuestro juicio, sean las adecuadas para llevar al Club hacia adelante y consolidar el impulso alcanzado. Durante todo este proceso, el enfoque de TFG seguirá siendo el mismo. Apoyaremos al Club en todo lo necesario para lograr el éxito en el terreno de juego y continuaremos nuestros esfuerzos para generar un impacto positivo en las comunidades a las que sirve el Club. TFG y el Club no harán más comentarios mientras duren estos trabajos. TFG ha contratado a Moelis & Company.
