articles.title: Man City charges: Enzo Maresca's first press conference after guilty verdict from independent Premier League commission
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca held his first press conference since Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules; Maresca spoke for 15 minutes on Friday ahead of their match against Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Q. You referred to the controversy surrounding City as noise. Is that somewhat dismissive of the genuine anger felt by many towards the findings of the commission? Do you understand the outrage and anger?

First of all, morning. I understand the reason why most of you are here. But the only thing I can say is stuff I already said. There is a process ongoing and, in this moment, I completely trust the club. This is what I can say about that.

Q. Why do you trust the club? Have you sought clarity from them? Have you seen the irrefutable evidence they refer to? Your predecessor, Pep Guardiola, once said if the club is relegated, he would stay. Will you give that commitment as well?

First of all, I trust the club because I trust the people and that is why I joined the club. There is not another club in the world where I would like to be. I'm very happy to be here. I'm very proud, I've said many times since I arrived.

Q. You were here before and you worked with Pep, do the achievements that you had then now look different to you?

Absolutely not. The last time I was here was the treble season. I know the effort from the players, the manager, the club. I know exactly the effort that the club gave to achieve that target. I don't have any doubts about that.

Q. Do you feel sympathy with the current squad?

The players, I've said already, we can only control the football side. We are focused on that. This is what we can do and control. We cannot control something different.

Q. Do you share the view of your CEO that there is a conspiracy against the club by the Premier League?

Again, I understand the reason why most of you are here, but the only thing I can say is what I said already that the reason why I joined the club is because I completely trust, 100 per cent, the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, all the organisation. I don't have any doubts about that.

Q. Have you had personal assurances from Sheikh Mansour?

I spoke with the club for sure. Probably the right moment to speak about that is when we're going to win this appeal.

Q. Have you spoken to Pep Guardiola since the ruling came out?

I spoke with Pep the last time after the Man Utd game, after the derby. That was the last time I spoke with Pep and I know that he's coming on Tuesday.

Q. What does it mean to you to know you have his support?

It's always a pleasure. After 10 years here, he can come at any time he wants, not just for a game, for a training session, at any moment. I think it will be nice for him, for the fans, for everyone.

Q. In May 2022, Pep said that if the club has lied to him, he'll walk away. Would that be the same for you? If it's confirmed, would you consider your position?

I just said, I would like to speak about this situation when we're going to win the appeal. For now, it makes no sense to speak about anything because I don't have much information. I understand the reason why most of you are here because you want to hear something.

Q. To a certain extent, shouldn't it be Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the chairman, or Ferran Soriano, the CEO, answering these questions, because really, as you're saying, it isn't too much to do with you?

Don't forget it's the Liverpool press conference.

Q. You said previously you trust the club totally at the moment, so could that change?

Sorry, that was a wrong answer. I completely trust the club in this moment, in the future, always. Thank you, I can modify the answer.

Q. With this hanging over you for weeks or months, how do you avoid that impacting the season?

You cannot avoid. We completely understand the seriousness of the situation. I'm not saying we don't understand that. We understand, the players understand, but it's our duty, our job to try to control the noise. The managers and the players are focused on winning games, not about something different.

Q. If the appeal is lost, what happens then?

And what happens the appeal is won, what happens then?

Q. I can imagine what happens if you win, but if you lose?

I don't know. We are predicting the future. I'm worried about tomorrow, two days, three days, I don't know what's happening in the future. The only thing I can say is that I think it's fair from my point of view, from all of us, that we respect the process. There is an appeal ongoing, we'll see what happens.

Q. Pep once said he'd be happy to manage in League One. It was a joke but he still said it. I think City fans would be very happy to hear you say the same.

I won the Championship with Leicester so in case of League One, we will see. But again, we are talking about something that we don't know.

Q. At England last week, Thomas Tuchel spoke about concerns that this will affect players psychologically on the City players that were with him. Do you share that?

Seeing the environment in the last two days inside the building, no, I'm not worried at all. The environment with the players is nice. In this moment, we are top of the league, we have every reason to be happy and excited.

Q. Before the international break you won at Old Trafford with 10 men. Is there a bigger test in the Premier League than Anfield?

It will be a tough game for sure, a tough test, as you've said. We need to be ready. The focus has to be about the game but we also know the environment at Anfield is nice and it will probably be even worse because of the situation. Again, it's our duty to do our best and win the game.

Q. In terms of what you learnt about your players at Old Trafford, do you have any doubts about them being able to face the pressure?

Absolutely they can face the pressure. Absolutely. We have players already that have already experienced similar situations. Enzo Fernandez has played in Argentina where almost every game is like going to Anfield. It's not a problem.

Q. You were here in 2022/23 when the charges were first announced and the team then went on to win the treble, how did the players and staff use that news to rally everyone together?

In this moment, it's also a matter of sticking together. As Erling said yesterday, it's true. This is the situation, this is the noise. The most important thing is we continue to do the right things. We are on the same page with the players, the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, the fans. We need to have the passion from our fans, their voice. Hopefully at the end we can celebrate a good win.

Q. Can you lean on your leaders, Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias, to carry the dressing room?

Yeah, they need to help their team-mates. They are doing that. But again, I understand you probably want to hear different words from me but the real words is that the players…yes the noise is there but they are 20, 25 years old. They come, they enjoy the training session, they go home happy, they are top of the league. So the players are relaxed. They are just thinking about how we can beat Liverpool and we are going to try.

Q. You were here before under Pep, can you remember how you handled that at that moment to keep them altogether?

Exactly in the same way. Just try to manage to noise. We understand the seriousness of the situation. We understand the noise completely, 100 per cent it's something serious. But we just need to manage that and focus on what we can do and what we can control. That is to try to prepare the game in the best way and go to Anfield and win the game.

Q. If the commission's findings were published before you joined the club, would you still have agreed to become manager?

Again, I know the organisation from years ago. I know how serious they are. I know they do the right things. I would like to speak about this when we're going to win the appeal.

Q. When joining, did you or them raise the subject of the charges?

No, to be honest. We did not speak about that because I don't think that was a problem for the club at the time. Also because they are thinking in an honest way. I think they are convinced that at the end we are going to win the appeal.

Finally! He's good. He went to Marbella, two, three days off. He played golf, recovery and ready for Anfield. He's good. Thank you.

Q. You were interviewed as part of similar situation in respect of charges in Italy. What was that experience like and what can you learn from that experience?

It's quite a different situation. The players are just thinking about the game and how they can get better. It's a different situation.

I trust the club because I know the people. But I promise you that my focus is just about football. I'm not thinking about different things. I don't understand many things, I just focus on the things I can control which is the football side.

articles.title: ESPN College GameDay 2026 Location, TV Schedule and Week 6 Predictions
articles.summary: Last week, ESPN's College GameDay took a break from the SEC to focus on a marquee Big Ten matchup between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Iowa Hawkeyes. This week, though, it'll be back to SEC action for a matchup that should have significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications.
articles.body:
Last week, ESPN's College GameDay took a break from the SEC to focus on a marquee Big Ten matchup between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Iowa Hawkeyes. This week, though, it'll be back to SEC action for a matchup that should have significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications.

Sixth-ranked Alabama is set to host second-ranked Georgia in one of the biggest matchups of the college football season to date. College GameDay will be in Tuscaloosa during the day to help set the stage.

Here's what you need to know for the GameDay broadcast and the week's headline matchup.

Venue: Denny Chimes on the University of Alabama campus in Tuscaloosa

Crew: Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, and Nick Saban

Saturday's matchup should be one of the top college games of the season and is arguably the most anticipated since Lane Kiffin and LSU visited Mississippi in Week 3. The Bulldogs and the Crimson Tide each carry a 5-0 record into the game, along with the look of legitimate title contenders.

Georgia's offense ranks first in the nation in scoring, with an average of 51.4 points. Led by quarterback Gunner Stockton, running back Nate Frazier, and a bevy of difference-makers, the Bulldogs have regularly raced up and down the field in the early season.

Defensively, Georgia is no slouch either. The Bulldogs have surrendered an average of only 13.4 points this season.

While the Bulldogs might be the most complete team in college football right now, Alabama is a dangerous and familiar foe. The Crimson Tide rank second in scoring (49.6 points per game) and have surrendered just 20.8 points per game. Kalen DeBoer's squad will also have a massive home-field advantage.

Of course, it's unclear what sort of environment Georgia and Alabama will see on Saturday, if they face off as scheduled. Adverse weather conditions resulting from Hurricane Isaias could impact the game, though both sides are preparing as normal.

"It's uncertainty. [It's] beyond my control," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said, per Jordan D. Hill of 247Sports. "We as coaches game plan for multiple situations—weather conditions—when they're there. We had that same prep last week with the threat of those things. Doesn't change a lot about practice."

Georgia won convincingly when these two teams last faced, claiming a 28-7 victory in last year's SEC Championship Game. However, the Crimson Tide have won both regular-season meetings since DeBoer took over in 2024.

The prediction here is that weather conditions do take some of the proverbial air out of the offenses. In a bit of a defensive struggle between the SEC powerhouses, a raucous crowd and a few untimely mistakes by Stockton hand Alabama a close victory.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Maresca says Premier League club will win appeal
articles.summary: Coach says he has absolute faith in Man City despite guilty finding over breaches of Premier League financial rules.
articles.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says he has absolute faith the club will win its appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

In his first news conference since the bombshell announcement last week, the Italian on Friday also rejected any suggestion that City’s haul of silverware over the past 15 years was now tainted.

“I completely trust the club,” said Maresca, who was appointed manager in June but also previously worked at City as part of Pep Guardiola’s coaching staff.

“I trust the club because I trust the people, and this is also the reason why I joined the club. … There is not another club in the world where I would like to be.”

An independent commission found that City had arranged “sham” contracts with a number of their commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.2bn) over nine seasons from 2009 to 2018.

The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, are appealing against the judgement .

They likely face a severe points penalty that could lead to relegation or even expulsion from the Premier League if they fail to overturn the verdict.

“The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust 100 percent the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, all the organisation. So I don’t have any doubt about that,” Maresca said.

“I spoke with the club for sure, and we all [have] trust, and the right moment to speak about that is when we win this appeal.”

Since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008, City have become the dominant force in English football.

They have won eight Premier League titles, the Champions League and multiple other trophies over the past 15 years.

Maresca, whose side have won all five of their Premier League games this season, rejected the suggestion that those previous successes were now tainted.

“Absolutely not,” the former Chelsea boss said. “I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep.

“So I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target.”

Maresca to welcome Guardiola’s first return to Man City

Guardiola stepped down at the end of last season after a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad Stadium.

City travel to Liverpool on Sunday for their first outing since the guilty finding, and Guardiola is set to attend their next home game against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

“After 10 years here, he can come at any time he wants,” Maresca said. “I think it would be nice for him. It would be nice for the fans, for everyone.”

Maresca had spoken to City’s in-house media on Thursday and said the current players “ don’t care too much about the noise ” currently surrounding the club.

The new head coach and his players, however, are set for a hostile reception when they travel to Anfield, the home of their fierce rivals, but Maresca said his players would stay focused on the match.

“Probably [it] will be even more warm in terms of environment. But the reason why I decided to be manager is for this kind of game,” he said.

“I’m not worried at all. Again, the environment is from the players. It’s nice.

“In this moment, we are top of the league, so the players have all the reasons to be happy and excited.”

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Mourinho lashes out at ‘ridiculous’ criticism of Mbappe
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe takes fire for how he has chosen to recover from knee injury as he prepares to return for Real Madrid.
articles.body:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho has slammed criticism of star striker Kylian Mbappe, calling the attacks “ridiculous”.

The French captain has come under fire for spending his time recovering from a left knee injury in France and Switzerland rather than Madrid. He suffered a hyperextension of the joint while playing in a Nations League match against Turkiye on September 25.

The 27-year-old was also pictured at the entrance of a Parisian nightclub and photographed on a bicycle when he was in Switzerland.

Some fans claimed it was a deliberate snubbing of Mourinho, who only days before had said players should avoid skiing or riding bicycles to avoid injury.

“Are these criticisms over the top? They are ridiculous,” Mourinho said at a news conference on Friday on the eve of Real’s La Liga home match with Villarreal.

“All the players who were obliged to be present every day for their recovery were here.

“Mbappe came, like the others, to undergo scans in order to be diagnosed.

“He then went to see a specialist in France because he has history with his knee, which we cannot ignore.”

Mourinho, whose side lost to Atletico Madrid in their last match and already lag six points behind bitter rivals Barcelona, is never one to shy away from a confrontation and tackled each of the criticisms against Mbappe.

“Problems involving football are not sufficient for you,” the 63-year-old Portuguese coach told reporters.

“Therefore, you have raised the issue of the discotheque, which in fact was not one because it was used for a private event for Fashion Week.

“As for the bicycle in Switzerland, it was in a hotel made up of small houses which makes them available so guests can ride to the communal areas, and you would have us believe he was competing in the Tour of Switzerland.”

Mbappe, who returned to training on Wednesday, could feature on the pitch as early as Saturday. Mourinho shrugged off the potential of a hostile reception for Mbappe against Villarreal, reiterating that he was “certain” the all-time World Cup record goal scorer has fulfilled “his obligations to Real Madrid”.

It is not the first time this season that Mbappe has been subjected to attacks by fans.

The Ultras Sur, a Real Madrid supporters group linked to the far right and banned from the Santiago Bernabeu, took issue with him last month.

They were furious that before a Real Madrid match, Mbappe, alongside Vinicius Jr and fellow Frenchman Ibrahima Konate, partially rolled up T-shirts bearing the words “ We are all Ceutans “, which was intended to be a message of support for people in the Spanish territory bordering Morocco.

Ceuta, a Spanish North African exclave, has been grappling with a migration crisis .

Mbappe was also criticised earlier this season over his choice of a location for recovery from a previous injury, which led to an online “ Mbappe Out ” campaign by some Real fans.

articles.title: Southampton v Portsmouth: South coast derby talking points
articles.summary: BBC Sport breaks down the main narratives and talking points before the 74th south coast derby between Southampton and Portsmouth.
articles.body:
Over two highly competitive games last season neither Southampton nor Portsmouth could claim the derby day bragging rights they so desperately craved.

The first match at St Mary's ended as an anti-climatic scoreless draw before things took flight at Fratton Park later in the season.

Leo Scienza found the net and ran the entire length of the pitch to celebrate in front of the Saints fans prior to Ebou Adams heading a late equaliser home. He also ran the length of the field to salute the supporters in the Fratton End.

Southampton then ended their season with Spygate dominating proceedings after Pompey had secured their status as a Championship side.

With the two bitter rivals set to reignite their rivalry on Sunday (12:00 BST), will one finally triumph in the south coast derby?

The lead-up to this south coast derby has been unlike any other.

While most spectators usually long for the day of the game, everyone connected with Southampton has been anxiously waiting for a verdict on the future of their head coach.

Finally on Wednesday they were put out of their misery when the FA announced that Tonda Eckert had been handed a suspended six-week ban and fined £28,000 for his role in the Spygate scandal. Crucially, this meant he could be in the dugout for Sunday's game at St Mary's and beyond.

Just minutes after the announcement, Saints posted a video , external on their social media channels of Eckert cheering with supporters.

"I think this news will be a little shot in the arm for them before the derby," said former Saints striker James Beattie.

"As a player that's one less thing to worry about and it frees you up to focus on the game. The lads are human at the end of the day and it would have been playing on their minds a little bit.

"Now it's been sorted they can look forward. The timing of the decision couldn't be better and hopefully they can go on and put in a really good performance at St Mary's."

Despite the lacklustre nature of the game, last season's derby still had an incredibly intense and hostile atmosphere.

With the Portsmouth fans undoubtedly having plenty of new verbal ammunition to fire at their rivals, Southampton supporters will be able to reply safe in the knowledge their manager will not be going anywhere soon.

'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal

One aspect that underpins the intensity and ferocity of this derby is how few times the teams have played each other, meaning each game feels like a genuine occasion.

Since 1996 they have met just 12 times across all competitions, with eight being a Premier League or Championship fixture.

Neither side has beaten the other in a league game since 2005, when Pompey thumped Saints 4-1 at Fratton Park.

Lomana LuaLua won a penalty and scored two goals in less than half an hour at Fratton Park in a famous day for the blue side of Hampshire.

The four league games since then have all ended even, alongside an FA Cup win for Portsmouth in 2010 and a convincing Southampton victory in their 2019 League Cup campaign.

Derogatory songs about either side are regular fixtures in their weekly matchday repertoires, so when they finally meet supporters get the chance to unleash their jibes towards the other side.

Last season's derbies were the first league meetings since 2012 and were very highly anticipated by the supporters who sang "we're coming for you" in the games prior.

With the frustration of neither winning carrying over to this season, Sunday's game will no doubt make for an intense atmosphere.

Inside the bitter rivalry between Saints and Pompey

Have Portsmouth's big signings made an impact?

This summer was a significant one for Portsmouth, with John Mousinho and sporting director Rich Hughes operating with an increased transfer budget.

Pompey spent more than £10m on additions, significantly more than in previous seasons under Mousinho.

They had not spent more than £1.5m on a single player for about 15 years but this summer they went over that threshold four times on forwards Marko Milovanovic and Tyrese Shade, winger Abu Kamara and midfielder Rocco Shein.

Milovanovic has impressed in spells but struggled with a number of fitness issues and has not played in Portsmouth's last two matches.

The 6ft 6in player has scored twice in the Championship this season and when fit appears to be Mousinho's preferred choice up front.

Shein looked to be a classy addition in his Portsmouth debut when he shone at London Stadium in the first half of Pompey's eventual EFL Cup defeat by West Ham.

He has since played in all seven of their league matches in a deeper midfield position, mostly alongside captain Marlon Pack.

Kamara and Shade have both shown promise but are yet to make a statement on the pitch this season, registering an assist each across their opening games since arriving.

Away from their permanent additions one attacker who has caught the eye is Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, on loan from Chelsea.

The 17-year-old winger has already proven that despite his age he is more than ready for this level, scoring and assisting once this season.

In early September, Kavuma-McQueen suffered a double fracture on his right hand but opted against surgery to continue playing with a splint on his arm, making for a longer recovery period.

This was a decision that appeared to impress head coach Mousinho who labelled the forward as a player and person that "ticks all the boxes".

Transfer window thoughts as Portsmouth spend £10m

Eckert's side have started the season well, especially at home with a perfect four wins from four and an impressive 15 goals scored.

Southampton began the season on negative four points but have motored up to 10 points after eight games.

They have beaten Stoke City, Millwall, Swansea and Bristol City handsomely at St Mary's with playmakers Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza playing big roles alongside the division's top scorer Cyle Larin.

The Canada international is a clear and present danger but perhaps the best way Pompey can prevent him making in an impact is by stopping, or at least limiting, his supply line.

Azaz in particular has impressed with his three goals and five assists in eight Championship matches.

The 26-year-old has developed into one of Saints' most important attackers, and one of the Championship's best advanced midfielders, since joining from Middlesbrough in the summer of 2025.

He tends to line-up in the number 10 position of Eckert's 4-2-3-1 formation, just behind the striker and in between the wingers.

Azaz provided the assist for Southampton's opening goal of the derby at Fratton Park last season and he'll be hoping to make a similar impact for Saints on Sunday.

Scienza has continued to look dangerous after last season's breakout campaign where he was named Southampton's player of the season with 17 Championship goal contributions.

Portsmouth have kept two clean sheets out of their seven games this season and will have to defend at their best if they are to keep the Saints attack out.

articles.title: Watch Never-Before-Seen Video of Nick Saban Benching Jalen Hurts for Tua in CFP Title Game
articles.summary: As part of ESPN's Saban documentary series about Nick Saban's life and career, the network released never-before-seen footage of his decision to replace Jalen Hurts with Tua Tagovailoa in the College Football Playoff National Championship Game against Georgia on Jan. 8, 2018.
articles.body:
As part of ESPN's Saban documentary series about Nick Saban's life and career, the network released never-before-seen footage of his decision to replace Jalen Hurts with Tua Tagovailoa in the College Football Playoff National Championship Game against Georgia on Jan. 8, 2018.

Saban explains in the clip he knew it "was the time" to make the change at halftime when Alabama was trailing 13-0 with Hurts having thrown for just 21 yards.

Hurts admits later in the clip that he "can't say that I was surprised" about the benching. His voice trails off and there is a long pause before it cuts back to Saban.

"He's a competitor," Saban says in a talking head segment about Hurts. "He wants to play. He wants to do well. No different than anybody else that ever played the sport. Nobody wants to be insignificant, but I didn't make that decision in two minutes. I made it in two minutes, but I thought about it for two months. You don't just make emotional decisions like, 'I'm really frustrated we're not moving the ball right now, so I'm gonna change quarterbacks.' No, it was calculated."

Hurts previously struggled in the regular-season finale against Auburn. He finished 12-of-22 for 112 yards and one touchdown in a 26-14 loss that kept Alabama out of the SEC Championship Game.

The Crimson Tide made the College Football Playoff as the final entrant in the No. 4 spot thanks largely to previously-undefeated Wisconsin losing to two-loss Ohio State in the Big Ten Championship Game.

Hurts wasn't great in the semifinal against Clemson with 120 passing yards on 24 attempts, but Alabama's defense was dominant with just 188 yards allowed and two interceptions.

Tagovailoa, a 5-star recruit in the 2017 class, threw a total of 53 passes in eight appearances prior to the title game. He finished 14-of-24 for 166 yards, three touchdowns and one interception against Georgia.

Alabama scored on five of eight possessions with Tagovailoa at quarterback. He threw a 41-yard touchdown pass to DeVonta Smith in overtime after Georgia settled for a field goal to give the Crimson Tide a 26-23 win.

articles.title: El milagro de Valverde
articles.standfirst: El capitán, con un esguince de grado 3 desde el derbi del 20 de septiembre, entra en la convocatoria tras una recuperación sin precedentes
articles.summary: Tras la lesión en el derbi, el pasado lunes se sometió al test Course Navette sobre el césped de Valdebebas, una prueba de resistencia
articles.body: El Real Madrid mantuvo en vilo todo lo que pudo la reaparición de Fede Valverde... hasta que hizo pública la lista de convocados para el partido frente al Villarreal. El capitán, que cayó lesionado en el derbi ante el Atlético, completó el último entrenamiento sin problemas por lo que, tras 17 días de baja desde el último parte, está a disposición de Mourinho para el primer partido tras el parón de selecciones. El origen de la lesión está en el derbi del pasado 20 de septiembre, que el Madrid perdió por 2-1 en el Metropolitano. El uruguayo sufrió una dura entrada de Kang-in Lee en la primera mitad, una acción que, junto a un pisotón de Cuti Romero sobre Bellingham, centró las críticas del club al arbitraje del encuentro. Pese al golpe, Valverde completó el partido y fue a su término cuando saltaron las alarmas, ya que terminó con la zona realmente hinchada. El club emitió dos comunicados sobre su estado. En el primero, nada más acabar el derbi, informó de que el centrocampista sufría "un traumatismo severo en el tobillo izquierdo". Dos días después, el 22 de septiembre, tras nuevas pruebas, precisó el diagnóstico definitivo: "un esguince de grado 3 en el tobillo izquierdo", dejándolo "pendiente de evolución". En la semana del regreso al trabajo en Valdebebas, que coincidió con la primera del parón, llegó la primera señal alentadora. Valverde completó, junto a varios de sus compañeros, un test de esfuerzo sobre el césped, una prueba física que midió la resistencia y el estado de forma de la plantilla, y en la que el uruguayo pudo volver a trotar sobre el verde, indicio de que su tobillo ya respondía a las exigencias de la carrera. En los días posteriores, el capitán alternó ese trabajo de campo con sesiones de gimnasio. Esa combinación se mantuvo durante toda la semana. Mourinho contó con el Real Madrid 'C' para disputar un par de partidillos de entrenamiento con un grupo reducido del primer equipo, un ejercicio en el que Valverde no participó, pues seguía con su trabajo específico. El paso más visible llegó el 7 de octubre, 17 días después de la lesión, cuando el capitán reapareció en los medios del club en la foto de un acto previo al entrenamiento en la que se le veía de corto y con botas, señal inequívoca de estaba listo para rendir sobre el verde. Esa misma jornada volvió a tocar balón. Ayer, a dos días del duelo ante el Villarreal, el club trasladó que sería en la sesión previa (hoy) al partido cuando se despejara si Valverde llegaba o no al regreso liguero ante los groguets. El último esguince en el que el Madrid especificó el grado, también un grado 3, fue el de Dani Ceballos el 1 de septiembre de 2024, y el utrerano acabó estando 33 días de baja. Por otro lado, Mourinho ya trabajó con normalidad con los internacionales que se incorporaron los últimos días, mientras que Mbappé se encuentra en perfecto estado y su titularidad ante el Villarreal está asegurada.

articles.title: 'Not Celtic' - O'Neill condemns Desmond protest as ultras boycott
articles.summary: "This is not Celtic at all," is manager Martin O'Neill's response to the rising tensions between sections of the fan base and the club's board.
articles.body:
"This is not Celtic at all," was manager Martin O'Neill's response to the rising tensions between sections of the fan base and the club's board.

The Green Brigade has announced plans to boycott Scottish Cup matches and home European ties, with the ultras group saying: "The disconnect between those who control Celtic and those who support it has never felt greater.

"Under the influence of Dermot Desmond, a dark cloud lingers over our club creating an increasingly unsustainable environment."

Desmond, the club's largest shareholder, was recently the target of a protest during the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews.

Celtic responded with the threat of an "indefinite ban" on anyone "established to be involved in planning, facilitating or participating" in the incident.

The club has also chosen to no longer recognise the Celtic Fans Collective as a representative body.

"I came into this situation this time last year and it seems to be going back to that again," O'Neill said, referencing previous anti-board sentiment.

"I don't agree at all with what happened up at St Andrews. I don't agree with that at all.

"I mean, we derided Rangers [ultras] in the [last season's Scottish Cup] game for wearing balaclavas and then suddenly we're doing it ourselves. This is not Celtic at all."

The Celtic Fans Collective is a coalition of supporter groups, including the Green Brigade.

Referring to the club's "latest irrational statement", the Green Brigade described it as "another attack on supporters" and said it demonstrates the "utter disdain they have for our group".

They also state their members had nothing to do with events in St Andrews, while commending those behind the stunt, which involved the throwing of tennis balls.

O'Neill called the boycott "a really sad situation" before adding: "But we went through it last season."

The veteran manager continued: "I can remember the days of having 80,000 people in Seville [2003 Uefa Cup final] without an arrest, that's Celtic to me.

"Or the final whistle going in the last match of the season, where the crowd come onto the pitch and that's like a euphoric state. Those are phenomenal memories which I'll never forget.

"All I do know is that when the club were together towards the end of the season, I genuinely felt we were unbeatable."

articles.title: Bordalás: “¿Carvajal? Entiendo la pregunta pero mi mente está en el partido contra el Barcelona”
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón comparecía en la previa del partido frente al FC Barcelona y respondía al interés azulón en el ex del Real Madrid
articles.summary: El técnico azulón comparecía en la previa del partido frente al FC Barcelona y respondía al interés azulón en el ex del Real Madrid
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa en la previa del duelo frente al FC Barcelona. El técnico alicantino no quiso hablar del supuesto interés del cuadro azulón en Dani Carvajal y señaló que el equipo tiene que estar “mentalizado” de cara al choque contra los de Hansi Flick. Carvajal: “Entiendo perfectamente tu pregunta y la respeto, pero no voy a hablar nada de este tema porque mi mente está en el partido de mañana frente al FC Barcelona”. Satriano: “Puede llegar, ha estado entrenando con normalidad hoy. No me gusta dar pistas peor ojalá podamos contar con él”. Tras el parón: “Han llegado bastante bien, algunos un poco cansados del viaje, del cambio horario y demás. Somos optimistas. El resto están bien. Vestuario: “El descanso les ha venido bien, a nivel físico y mental, han sido unas semanas muy estresantes. Después de lo que nos venía, ahora llega un calendario ajustado, les ha venido bien. Les veo con ganas. Durante toda la semana les he estado repitiendo que lo primero que hay que tener para afrontar un partido como el de mañana es tener una buena actitud. Para sacar un buen resultado tenemos que tener una atención máxima, es uno de los mejores equipos a nivel mundial. Carrera: “Lo comentaban hace nada, ni yo mismo era consciente de la cantidad de partidos que he dirigido. He disfrutado mucho, hasta el momento, sigo disfrutando de esta profesión, del fútbol, esto ha sido gracias a los clubes donde he estado, presidentes, jugadores y directivos que han hecho que pueda alcanzar estos números que son impresionantes, no era consciente de ello. Vamos a seguir dando alegrías a nuestra afición”. Nueve partidos en un mes: “Como dije, entiendo y respeto profundamente, es lo que debéis hacer por lo que ha trascendido, pero tenéis también que respetar que, a tan pocas horas, tenemos que centrarnos en el partido de mañana. Tenemos jugadores con muchos minutos, iremos regulándolos, dar el descanso necesario a los que podamos e intentar competir al máximo para ir sacando puntos en partidos que no van a ser sencillos”. Expulsiones: “Sin duda, quedarte en inferioridad ha sido un hándicap desde que empezó el campeonato. Yo insisto ahora y siempre, intentar no cometer ningún error e intentar, dentro de nuestras posibilidades, evitar cualquier acción que se nos pueda juzgar enormemente”. Barcelona: “Es uno de los equipos en mejor estado de forma del campeonato e incluso de Europa. Jugadores en un estado de forma brutal. No lo achacaría a si es el mejor o no, siempre se compara, pero lo que llevo diciendo hace años es que el fútbol ha cambiado, el FC Barcelona tiene jugadores de un nivel técnico increíble, pero a nivel físico el fútbol ha cambiado muchísimo. El Barça me gusta mucho con balón, pero me gusta mucho sin balón, en ello también es el mejor equipo de LaLiga”. Mejor momento para ir al Camp Nou: “Siempre es complicadísimo, ahí están los números, no me los invento yo. La diferencia de un club a otro es abismal. De todo. Es muy difícil, muchas veces algunos compañeros preguntan. No se ha ganado al Barça en tantos años porque es tremendamente difícil. Mi equipo siempre afronta los partidos sabiendo las dificultades, pero sabiendo lo que debemos hacer para sacar un buen resultado. Intentamos tener una mentalidad ambiciosa, ganadora y consciente de las dificultades que vamos a tener”. Plantilla culé: “El Barça tiene una plantilla increíble, puede doblar posiciones y no se nota, y lo estamos comprobando. En los once, en los cambios de partido, nunca se resiente el equipo cuando hay variaciones o cambios. Como amante del fútbol no quitaría a nadie, lo que ocurre es que habría que quitar a todos y eso es imposible”. Borja Mayoral: “Bien, está entrenando con normalidad. Es consciente de que tiene que dar un paso al frente, mejorar sus prestaciones y ayudar al equipo. Le exijo como a todos, él debe ser un jugador importante y tiene que mejorar su nivel y prestaciones, ojalá lo consiga porque lo merece el equipo, él y los compañeros”. Raphinha: “Que no esté no tiene que ser un problema. Es un jugador en un momento de forma increíble, ha hecho doce goles, es espectacular el comienzo que ha tenido y la repercusión, pero el Barça tiene una plantilla increíble. Tiene un nivel mundial, todos son internacionales”. Imponer sus ideas en el Camp Nou: “Es importante que entendamos el juego, que tienes que estar durante el partido los noventa minutos con los cinco sentidos, no puedes cometer errores groseros o graves, no puedes tener pérdidas en zonas de riesgo. Tienes que entender sin duda e interpretar bien el partido porque el Barça, si te equivocas, te puede pintar la cara, como se dice vulgarmente. Los jugadores lo han entendido, mañana vamos a tener una gran respuesta en cuanto a actitud y ser solidarios. Soy optimista y ojalá mañana podamos plantarle cara a un grandísimo equipo como es el FC Barcelona”. Lamine Yamal y ataque del Barça: “Es muy difícil porque estabas nombrando jugadores con grandísimo nivel. Va a ser muy difícil frenarlo, pero vamos a intentar hacer un gran partido, ser muy serios, jugar sin ningún tipo de complejos. Lamine es un magnífico jugador, lo está demostrando, es muy joven. No se puede decir si es el mejor del mundo, hay grandísimos jugadores, él tiene una carrera por delante muy larga. Podría conseguirlo sin duda por el potencial que tiene”.

articles.title: Fer López saca las 'garras': "Me pusieron en una posición que me ayuda a jugar como lo hago ahora"
articles.standfirst: El ex del Celta suma cinco goles y dos asistencias en Segunda con el Wolverhampton
articles.summary: El ex del Celta suma cinco goles y dos asistencias en Segunda con el Wolverhampton
articles.body: La primera temporada de Fer López (Madrid, 2004) en la Premier no fue como esperaba. Ni mucho menos. En noviembre, al poco de llegar, el ex del Celta, fichado por 23 millones de euros, vio cómo el Wolverhampton prescindía de Vítor Pereira. Una destitución -apenas registró una asistencia en 364 minutos de juego- que precipitó su regreso al Celta, cedido, en el mercado invernal. En Vigo acumuló minutos (1.432), marcó dos goles -uno espectacular contra el Estrella Roja en Europa League- y repartió una asistencia. En verano, de vuelta al Molineux, le tocó aceptar la nueva realidad del Wolverhampton, descendido a Segunda división. Lejos de resignarse, el español, internacional sub 21, ha sacado las 'garras'. Sus cinco goles -cuatro en Liga y uno en Copa de la Liga- en nueve partidos mantienen a los 'lobos' en la 'zona noble' de la tabla: marchan cuartos con 14 puntos, a uno de West Ham y Middlesbrough y a tres del sorprendente Swansea, líder. Sólo el exmallorquinista Cyle Larin (Southampton/7 goles), Will Lankshear (Middlesbrough/6) y Mo Touré (Norwich City/5) superan las cuatro dianas de Fer López en el Championship. Acumula, además, dos asistencias. Tan bien está rindiendo ejerciendo de mediapunta en el 1-4-2-3-1 de César Peixoto que los aficionados de los 'lobos' suspiran por que la "molestia física" que le obligó a regresar antes de tiempo de la sub 21 no le impida estar ante el Middlesbrough. "Ningún aficionado de los Wolves querría afrontar un partido sin él, pero Fer López se ha convertido en un activo fundamental para los Wolves y es demasiado importante como para arriesgarse con él en esta etapa tan temprana de la temporada", sugiere la 'BBC'. No es de extrañar que fuera elegido 'Jugador del Mes' de agosto en el Wolverhampton. "Espero que vengan muchos más. Quiero agradecer al cuerpo técnico por creer en mí. Me pusieron en una posición que me ayudó a jugar como lo hago ahora. Él míster quiere jugar al fútbol y yo necesito jugar en equipos que quieran ser propositivos con el balón, que quieran tener la posesión, así que estoy contento con eso”, reconocía Fer López. Peixoto, ex jugador del Espanyol, también se mostró encantado con el ex del Celta tras la victoria ante el Preston (3-1): "Tuvo una actuación increíble. Hace un gran trabajo y tiene mucha calidad. Su reto es mantener ese nivel durante los 90 minutos y sentirse cómodo con la idea del juego". Los Wolves han sumado un nuevo 'lobo' a la 'manada': 'Súper' López.

articles.title: 6 Managers Already on the Hot Seat Around Europe
articles.summary: A three-week international break is a nightmare for any club manager. If things have been going well, the interruption could have ruined all that momentum. Those off to a bad start, meanwhile, have been left waiting to try to turn things around.
articles.body:
A three-week international break is a nightmare for any club manager. If things have been going well, the interruption could have ruined all that momentum. Those off to a bad start, meanwhile, have been left waiting to try to turn things around.

For the managers on the tougher end of that scale, the wait is finally over. The issue with being in the hot seat, though, is that the recovery doesn't always work out, and clubs are rarely shy about pulling the trigger when enough is enough.

The following six managers could all face some serious questions if results don't improve soon. While not an exhaustive list of coaches under pressure, these are some of the more intriguing situations around Europe as domestic play resumes.

Did we miss anyone? Let us know in the comments on the B/R App!

No wins in five games, along with scoring just two goals, would have any manager's seat feeling toasty. After being allowed to spend more than $400 million over the summer, though, Roberto De Zerbi should really be feeling the heat.

Spurs' latest rebuild was never likely to be smooth sailing, but De Zerbi made some risky decisions entering the season, and the results so far speak for themselves.

Antonin Kinsky became the team's starting goalkeeper after largely serving as the backup for the previous 18 months, during which he made several high-profile errors. While it would be unfair to blame the 23-year-old for the eight league goals Spurs have conceded so far, he hasn't been convincing either.

At the other end of the pitch, Richarlison was omitted from the Premier League squad entirely, leaving Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush as the only options up front. Solanke has looked short on fitness and confidence, and Marmoush has offered more of a threat playing from wide.

In midfield, De Zerbi has struggled to find a workable combination despite sanctioning a $240 million-plus revamp, signing Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, and never starting the same trio in consecutive games across all competitions.

There's still time to turn things around, but it will be interesting if things haven't improved by the time January approaches. There will be pressure to spend money once again, and Spurs may decide that they can't keep writing checks to fund a failing project.

This time last season, Marseille were gearing up to start a Champions League campaign with a trip to face Real Madrid. Now, they're second-to-last in Ligue 1 and on a five-game losing streak in all competitions.

Bruno Genesio arrived in the summer, but it seems he wasn't fully aware of the scope of the challenge. Marseille's ownership has set about slashing the budget, and the only arrivals have been Timothy Weah and Hamed Traore, who were both on loan at OM last season.

Goal.com's Krishan Davis documented the issues between Genesio and ownership, which have seen the manager publicly question the club's strategy on multiple occasions. French newspaper L'Équipe has reported that Genesio is unlikely to make it past Christmas, but Marseille's financial situation may even prevent them from paying the agreed compensation.

If that sounds untenable to you, that's probably because it would sound untenable to anyone. Marseille may be hoping Genesio simply leaves of his own accord to avoid having to pay him to do so, but however the situation is resolved, it feels unlikely to go on much longer.

Alarm bells started ringing for Alvaro Arbeloa less than a minute into his first competitive game. Just 31 seconds in, Chelsea's Joao Pedro burst through a huge gap between Fulham's centre-backs and lifted the ball over goalkeeper Bernd Leno to give his team the lead.

Those defensive issues continued throughout that 3-2 loss and into defeats to Sunderland and Crystal Palace. In those first three games , Fulham conceded seven times from over six expected goals, according to FotMob. Arbeloa's tactics could be described as aggressive, or, if you were less generous, as naïve.

After then having to answer questions about cryptic social media messages from a few players appearing to suggest dissatisfaction in the squad, it seemed Arbeloa's stay in West London would be a short one.

Following consecutive draws with Liverpool and Manchester United, however, things don't look quite so bleak. New signing David Affengruber has made an impact in defence after coming into the team for both of those games, while 19-year-old academy product Josh King looks capable of being a significant contributor this season.

Striker Gonzalo Garcia is also top 10 in the Premier League in expected goals, according to FotMob . While he has underperformed relative to that total (one goal scored to 2.3 expected), there are signs that more could come for him and Arbeloa.

If results don't pick up soon, though, Fulham may need to make a decision if relegation becomes a serious threat.

Pierre Sage felt like a logical pick for Crystal Palace to succeed Oliver Glasner. In a single season at Lens, he guided them to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 after they had finished midtable the previous year. He also won the Coupe de France, securing the club's first major honor since 1999.

With one win and a draw from five league games with Palace, though, pressure is starting to build. Even the 3-2 win at Fulham raised concerns, as Palace benefited from some disastrous defending by the home side to steal the three points.

A key selling point for Sage, in addition to his achievements in France, was his frequent use of wing-backs. That could have made for a smooth transition from Glasner's wing-back system, but it hasn't played out that way.

It is worth noting, though, that Glasner's team won just four Premier League games from mid-December. This was arguably a group in decline long before Sage's arrival, with a victory in the Europa Conference League at the end of last season masking many of those struggles.

It may be that this was simply a deceptively tougher job than some were willing to admit at the start of the season. The 0-0 draw with high-flying Leeds United prior to the international break was encouraging, though a victory over Glasner's Nottingham Forest in their first game after the break would go a long way toward stabilizing things for Sage.

"Worst 15 minutes I've ever seen." That was the assessment of former Manchester United player Gary Neville on Sky Sports commentary just before Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal that handed Fulham a second-half lead in a 1-1 draw before the international break.

While Neville is prone to hyperbole when it comes to the Red Devils, his criticism summed up the current sentiment around Michael Carrick's team. After guiding the team to a third-place finish last season, the 45-year-old has won just two of seven games in all competitions.

The early returns on the summer transfer work are also concerning. United didn't get involved in bidding wars for higher-priced midfielders as they set about rebuilding that position, but so far the trio of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba haven't made an impact, although the latter has been injured. That their arrivals also came at the cost of additions in defence and attack also looks to be an issue.

The biggest worry for United may be that their fixture schedule is about to get much busier. The team benefited from the extra rest that came with being out of Europe last season, but they're about to begin a run of eight games in under a month, starting with a home game against the hapless Tottenham Hotspur.

It could be the perfect opportunity to get things back on track for United and their manager. Anything but a win would really crank up the pressure, though.

Real Madrid have not made a disastrous start under Jose Mourinho, with two defeats and five victories putting them fourth in La Liga.

However, if history tells us anything, it's that the manager's seat at the Santiago Bernabéu is never cool. Those losses to Real Betis and Atlético Madrid also leave Los Blancos already six points behind Barcelona, and trailing their rivals by a considerable margin will never go down well with the club's leadership.

Mourinho does have Kylian Mbappe scoring at a goal-per-game pace in La Liga, and Jude Bellingham already has half as many goal involvements (five) as he had in all of last season. Vinicius Júnior only has one league goal, though, and Mourinho may be the next Real Madrid manager to struggle to make things work with both Mbappe and the Brazilian in the team.

The moment of truth for the early days of the 63-year-old's tenure should come on Oct. 25. The visit to Barcelona, who has already scored 31 league goals, will reveal whether this team is ready to compete with other European heavyweights both domestically and in the Champions League.

Victory there could see Mourinho win over his players in an instant, but defeat will likely lead to the same old questions about how far he can take a team aiming to compete for major honors.

articles.title: El juvenil Imga viaja a Vallecas y aspira a un debut especial
articles.standfirst: Aurtenetxe y Javi Martínez, campeón del mundo, los últimos que se estrenaron con 17 años
articles.summary: Aurtenetxe y Javi Martínez, campeón del mundo, los últimos que se estrenaron con 17 años
articles.body: El Athletic incluye en su convocatoria a Christian Imga, delantero internacional juvenil que viaja a Vallecas después de haberse sumado esta semana a los entrenamientos del primer equipo. Fichado del Alavés en edad cadete en el mercado de invierno de 2025 asegurándose un contrato de larga duración y cláusulas de mejora y ampliación, el potente extremo izquierdo aspira a un debut especial: sería el primer menor de edad en jugar en el Athletic desde que lo hicieron Aurtenetxe y Javi Martínez. Imga (Zumarraga, 2009) disfruta del primer equipo a causa de la lesión de Nico Williams, que fue baja en los dos últimos partidos de la selección española tras lesionarse en la victoria ante Croacia en el Pizjuán. El menor de los hermanos Williams será baja en Vallecas y la previsión es que empiece a entrenar con el grupo la próxima semana, aunque no está claro si podrá formar en la convocatoria para enfrentarse al Valencia. Djaló, que aparecía como una de las alternativas de la plantilla, regresó con gripe de su estadía con la selección de Guinea-Bisáu. La citación del joven extremo se produce pocos días después de que encandilara en sus primeros encuentros con la selección española sub18 que se proclamó campeona de la UEFA Friendship Cup. En ese torneo, además, fue distinguido como MVP.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick calls for speed and clarity over rivals' guilty verdict
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has called for a swift resolution to Man City's financial case, insisting "speed is essential" as he reflected on the potential impact on past Premier League title races; Man Utd take on Tottenham this Saturday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
An independent commission found City guilty of serious breaches of financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18, including arranging 'sham' commercial agreements to inflate revenues and reduce costs. The commission also upheld the majority of charges relating to the club's failure to co-operate with the Premier League's investigation.

City deny wrongdoing and have appealed against the findings, with the question of any potential punishment still to be decided.

Asked about the case, Carrick said: "I've got my own questions about it. It's affected me personally in different ways over a period of time.

"But as the case is going now, I don't know where that stands and how it's going to end up. So we'll just have to wait and see.

"What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted, I think for everyone's benefit, is essential."

The former Manchester United midfielder also reflected on the impact the case could have on the history of the Premier League, having experienced title races in which United finished behind City's teams.

However, Carrick insisted the emotions attached to competing for trophies could never be erased, regardless of what happens next.

"Regardless of anything, a medal anyway, in any sport in history, I think later on you get the medal and it's proved at different times," he said.

"It's the moment that you strive for, to win and achieve in that moment.

"So the medal here or there, not getting blown away, but that doesn't bring the feeling of whether you initially win or you don't win. That's essentially what we're all in for."

Carrick added that the uncertainty surrounding the case made a speedy conclusion particularly important, given the potential implications for clubs across the league.

"Speed is essential for everyone to be clear, to be able to deal with it, to be able to move on, whatever happens," he said.

"It's a unique situation to be in at this level, with such a huge impact in so many ways. So we all need to know what's going to happen."

What Premier League managers have said about the Man City verdict

"I'm not this kind of guy who blames someone with not enough information. Of course, I hear everything, I read everything, but I do not have all the information. I trust in the guys who are involved in these kinds of things and situations, and then we will see what happens. I'm a football coach, not a politician, and I love to be a football coach, and it should stay like this."

"I can't control anything from that. The only thing I can really focus on is our preparation, how we are doing, and therefore it is just a distraction, that is not in our hands. Hopefully it will be dealt with but I have enough topics to mention. But let's see how it goes. I heard there are still some ongoing processes so it is really difficult to say anything now."

"We've all seen the news. Obviously big news. Man City are appealing the situation, so what can you say when an appeal is going on? I'm not inside the story, I'm outside it completely. I played for Man City a long time ago, now for one year, but we'll wait and see what the result of the appeal is."

"It's not my topic, my topic is football and there are more qualified people to speak about this, so it is not my topic. It is not up to me and I was not involved in the title race in these years. I had different topics to deal with during this time when Manchester City won many titles. I think I just had one home game with them with Norwich, we won by the way, so I can't complain too much. It also makes no sense if right now everyone in the world wants to have opinions about this topic, there are more qualified people to talk about it. My topic is Leeds United."

"I think uncertainty is not good for anyone involved but there is the process ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end. No one knows what's going to happen. We have to focus on Liverpool and being the best club we can be, the best team we can be. That's my challenge. My opinion is not valid because I haven't spent that time and I haven't read as much as they've [the commission] done.

"I think the challenge of the game is so high that I don't think players think too much outside of this. They are thinking 'I have to mark this player' or 'I have to go and deal with this one' or 'I have be at this level because the level of the game is so high'. They will be focused on those things. Obviously they will have their own opinions but I think they will be fully focused on what happens on the pitch."

"I think as a manager of another club I am not able to judge. It's not my job in my job description to judge on that. There are authorities taking care of it. I think there is a clear process now, which we have followed and, for us, I am speaking on behalf of the whole club, it's the right approach to focus on what we can influence."

"It has been 24 hours a day. It was just City. I said, 'Ah, OK, this is the only problem in the world right now'. It's so big here in England, especially. And I wasn't here when all these things happened or did not happen, I don't know. To the appeal, there is no final verdict right now. That's why I don't see any point to comment on Man City because I can't. But let's say in general, if somebody cheats he needs to get punished. If not, then not. And of course, we all hope for the integrity of the game, for the integrity of the Premier League, that the final word is spoken soon.

"But we also know, and as I spoke earlier, I think there are thousands of pages to read, and I read a book every night, and it takes quite long to read thousands of pages and also then find the final verdict, so it takes a little bit of time. We have to be patient, but yes, it should be soon."

"There are still ongoing legal proceedings so it's not for me to comment on that. My position is simple: football has rules, on and off the pitch. You have to respect those rules, when they are broken they should have consequences otherwise it's not fair. We want fair competition, we want fair game, fair play, so the relevant authorities have to be relentless otherwise you lose the value of the competition. So we'll see.

"It happened 10 years ago, more or less. We were not here in Sunderland, for example. But it's about respecting rules so it's key because if you don't have fair competition it's a bit weird, so it's more or less the feeling we have in the building."

articles.standfirst: El conjunto dirigido por Cesc Fábregas quiere hacerse con el delantero del Rayo
articles.summary: El conjunto dirigido por Cesc Fábregas quiere hacerse con el delantero del Rayo
articles.body: Uno de los hombres que más está destacando este año en LaLiga es Sergio Camello, delantero del Rayo Vallecano que va a gol por partido, siete goles en siete encuentros, empatado en la tabla goleadora con futbolistas como Lamine Yamal o Kylian Mbappé. Eso ha provocado que desde las grandes ligas europeas el interés que existe desde hace tiempo, haya ido creciendo con el paso de las semanas. El Como es uno de los interesados por el '10' del Rayo, que acaba contrato en 2027, y no parece que vaya a renovar. Sin embargo, no será una operación fácil, ya que varios equipos intentarán hacerse con los servicios del delantero. Ahora es el Rayo el que tiene que actuar si quiere sacar algún beneficio de su salida. El futbolista que llegó el verano de 2023 a cambio de cinco millones de euros podría marcharse sin dejar un solo euro en las arcas del club. Por eso, los vallecanos deberían intentar venderlo en el mercado invernal para ingresar una cantidad, que a pesar de no ser lo máximo posible por la poca duración que le restará a su contrato en ese momento, será mejor que dejarlo marchar libre. Recibir aunque sea una parte menor, servirá para reforzar una posición en la que el equipo madrileño no va ni mucho menos sobrado. Sergio Camello es el delantero titular del conjunto vallecano, y el único reemplazo en la plantilla actualmente es Alemao. Por lo que el Rayo debe mover ficha ante la probable salida de su '10'. Cesc Fábregas está acostumbrado a 'pescar' talento en LaLiga. Algunos de los grandes ejemplos son Nico Paz, Assane Diao, Jesús Rodríguez, Jacobo Ramón o Luis Milla. articles.title: Alabama vs. Georgia Weather Update, Latest Forecast and Game Status amid Hurricane Isaias
articles.summary: Saturday night's massive SEC clash between the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs and No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, may avoid the wrath of Hurricane Isaias.
articles.body:
Saturday night's massive SEC clash between the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs and No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, may avoid the wrath of Hurricane Isaias.

According to The Weather Channel , Saturday's forecast for Tuscaloosa looks surprisingly tame at and around the time the game is scheduled to be played at 7:30 p.m. ET.

Although heavy rain and possible "tropical storm conditions" are expected throughout the morning, the chance of rain drops to 24 percent at around 10 a.m. and stays there until around 9 p.m. when it increases to a 36 percent chance of light rain.

Winds fewer than 10 mph are expected throughout the game as well, so that shouldn't be much of a factor either.

To this point, all signs suggest the game will be played as scheduled with no announced plans to change the time or location.

On Wednesday, Alabama Athletics released a statement on X, noting that the school was monitoring the weather and still planned to hold the game as scheduled:

As of Friday, The Weather Channel reported that Hurricane Isaias was a Category 3 hurricane located 240 miles south of Pensacola, Florida.

The expectation is that Hurricane Isaias will make landfall late Friday night from "Alabama to the western Florida Panhandle."

Hurricane Isaias is expected to "move farther inland and weaken" by Saturday, and radar appears to show it moving to the northern part of Alabama, just clear of Tuscaloosa.

Given the enormity of Saturday's game, the forecast comes as a major relief, as it doesn't appear rain and wind will have a significant impact.

Georgia and Alabama are tied atop the SEC right now with matching 3-0 conference records and 5-0 overall records, meaning the winner will have a huge advantage over the loser in terms of positioning for a potential SEC Championship Game berth.

articles.title: Estados Unidos-España: duelo de campeonas: "Entre nosotras no existen los amistosos"
articles.standfirst: Son las dos mejores potencias del ranking FIFA y las vigentes campeonas olímpica y del mundo
articles.summary: Son las dos mejores potencias del ranking FIFA y las vigentes campeonas olímpica y del mundo
articles.body: España y Estados Unidos, números 1 y 2 del ranking FIFA, se verán las caras este sábado (20:30 hora española) en el Audi Field de Washington en el primero de los dos amistosos que ambas potencias disputarán en esta ventana internacional en suelo americano. "Son dos partidos que van a ser muy competidos. Nos viene bien jugar contra selecciones de tantísimo mundial. No hay mejor escenario para ver nuestro nivel de cara al Mundial del próximo año", resumió Lucía Corrales, protagonista ante los medios en la previa. España es la vigente campeona del mundo, título que conquistó en 2023 y que luchará por revalidar en Brasil el próximo verano. De aquel equipo apenas hay 10 jugadoras en la actual convocatoria (de 25). Estados Unidos es la vigente campeona olímpica, medalla que conquistó en 2024 para engrosar un excelso palmarés en el que se advierten cuatro Mundiales; siete medallas olímpicas (cinco oros, una plata y un broce); o nueve torneos de la CONCACAF entre otros éxitos. "Son contextos totalmente diferentes. Ahora jugamos dos partidos amistosos en los que queremos probar estructuras diferentes y diversas maneras de jugar pensando en lo que viene el próximo verano que será apasionante. Queremos que todas las jugadoras tengan minutos. Para ambas selecciones no existen amistosos y saldremos a ganar", expuso Sonia Bermúdez en la previa. España y Estados Unidos parten, a ocho meses vista, como claros favoritos para la conquista del Mundial de Brasil. "Hay muchos rivales, no querría dejarme atrás a ninguno. Estados Unidos es una de las favoritas, pero venimos de jugar una fase final de la Nations contra rivales muy duros. Un Mundial es muy difícil de ganar porque un mal día te deja fuera. Hoy en día cualquier rival te estudia, te trabaja y no descartaría a nadie", resumió la seleccionadora española. España y Estados Unidos se han enfrentado en cuatro ocasiones hasta la fecha con un balance de una victoria española -en el último duelo entre ambas, en Pamplona en 2022-; y tres triunfos estadounidenses (Alicante 2019, Reims 2019 y Harrison 2020). "Hemos evolucionado mucho, tanto en clubes como en la selección", justificó Sonia, que cree tanto el progreso de la selección como del fútbol femenino es latente. "Estamos en un buen momento, siempre creciendo y seguir que en unos años será mejor", dijo. "Demandamos recursos, que cada vez están más cerca, y es cuestión de tiempo. La historia del fútbol masculino está lejos, pero estamos en el camino", añadió.

articles.title: David Moyes: Everton manager admits surprise at seeing the club being put up for sale by The Friedkin Group
articles.summary: Everton were put up for sale again on Friday; owners The Friedkin Group (TFG) have said they will only entertain interest from parties who they feel are the "right stewards to take the club forward"; TFG only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024
articles.body:
The Friedkin Group (TFG) announced they are open to new investment into the club - including the "potential sale of a controlling interest".

The group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin , only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 - ending Farhad Moshiri's long spell at the helm.

"Yeah I was surprised, they'd only came in a year and a half ago," Moyes said in a press conference - before claiming he first felt signs of the owners not being committed during the most recent transfer window.

"Most owners come in for a lot longer than that. We were all expecting them to be here for 20 to 30 years, however long it may be.

"But maybe the way things worked out over the transfer window, I probably had seen through it a little bit before that. It's probably all there for Evertonians to see now.

"I truly believed that with new ownership who were in for it completely with us all, my ambition coming back was to get Everton back to the levels they'd been at in the past - challenging for Europe more often, being around it.

"And probably you could tell with how I've been a lot over the summer that that's the way it's been. It's been a difficult summer for us.

"I only found out this morning myself along with everybody else. I'm a little bit surprised, but maybe not really that surprised."

Moyes also admitted he feels sympathy for the Everton fans who have to go through another period of uncertainty.

The last three years alone have seen Moshiri try to sell the club to 777 Partners and John Textor, only for both of their takeover bids to fall through. TFG also saw talks collapse before finally breaking through in late 2024.

Everton also had two rounds of points deductions for breaching the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR), which came in a period that nearly saw the club relegated from the Premier League for the first time.

Moyes, who returned to the club in early 2025, admitted the last year was one of stability for the club. But that has now changed.

Asked if he feels let down for being mis-sold a dream, Moyes said: "No. Because I love this club so much and they could have sold me anything and I'd have still taken it.

"But it's for Evertonians I feel sorry for the most. They've been through so many difficult periods, they really have. The last thing they wanted to hear was this.

"Last year we went through a season where there wasn't much drama. There wasn't any relegation problems, we had a bit of drama of money that we had to pay to Burnley.

"Apart from that, in the main we've done pretty well over the year and were just starting to get back at the right footing - and challenging at the right end of the table rather than the wrong end.

"I'm more disappointed for Evertonians who have to go through another period of: 'who's going to be the new owner?'"

Asked if he's concerned about his own future, with potential new owners set to arrive at the club, Moyes said: "I've not really thought about it yet from that point of view. The players have been great so far and we'll keep them focused on what we can do which is win the games.

"I always think that Evertonians galvanise even more so when it comes to a situation where the team needs help, the manager needs help - we'll stick together. We'll certainly be in that camp.

"I'm just reading the things that I've seen this morning. They're looking forward to getting the right people in to bring the club further forward.

"It's a great club if anybody is out there who wants to buy it. If they want to speak to me, I'll be the first person to tell them that it's certainly worth buying."

An Everton statement on Friday morning said: "When TFG became custodians of Everton, the club faced significant financial uncertainty and challenges both on and off the pitch.

"The immediate priority was to provide the stability, investment and support needed to secure the club's future, including helping to bring the long-promised stadium to completion for its deserving supporters.

"With that foundation now safely in place, the time is right to consider the next chapter for Everton. We will only entertain interest from parties who we strongly believe will be the right stewards to take the club forward and build on the momentum that has been established.

"Throughout this process, TFG's focus will remain unchanged. We will support the club in all ways necessary to achieve success on the pitch and will continue efforts to make a positive difference in the communities the club serves.

"TFG and the club will not be commenting further while this work is under way."

"It's not come as a big surprise to hear this news. When The Friedkin Group said a few months ago that they were looking for investors, the feeling and talk around Everton and the financial side of things that the club was actually up for sale. It was a sale they were looking for, rather than investors.

"One of the real reasons for this is TFG have probably come to a point where they have seen what it's going to cost to put Everton back at the top table of English football, which is where the club want to be and where they were a long number of years ago.

"That figure and cost implication is probably too much for them and they don't want to do that.

"From day one, there were rumours and mumblings that TFG weren't going to be at Everton for long. What they've been trying to do recently is put the club into a good financial situation, with a sale in mind.

"A lot of this also comes from the situation with Roma. They own Roma as well, they are building a new stadium there which will cost £1bn. In the end, it's all too much for them.

"I believe The Friedkin Group are looking for between £800m and £1bn to sell the club which will give them a tidy little profit, as they bought the club for cheaper than they should have done.

"It was interesting when you read the statement from The Friedkin Group saying: 'We will be fully committed to supporting the team on the pitch'. Well it didn't look that way in the summer transfer window, that's for sure. It was a bit of a disaster in the end.

"Although you have to remember the squad they had is a good squad, but a weak squad. If David Moyes was to get injuries with his players, then that squad would be tested. There's no two ways about that.

"The first squad he has at the moment is a very good, strong squad. But you could see that they were willing to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest. That said a lot about the investment and what they were doing.

"The only reason he didn't go was because the crowd made their feelings known. That pressure forced The Friedkin Group to reconsider selling him as he's one of the young bright talents of Everton."

articles.title: ‘It’s affected me personally’: Man United boss Carrick calls for swift resolution to Man City’s financial case
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has called for a swift resolution to Manchester City's long-running financial charges case, admitting that
articles.body: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has called for a swift resolution to Manchester City's long-running financial charges case, admitting that the controversy has raised several questions and affected him personally.Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Carrick said the uncertainty surrounding the case had gone on long enough, stressing that a conclusion would benefit everyone involved in English football.“Very difficult to say in many ways,” Carrick said when asked about the charges against City.“It's thrown up a lot of questions, some have had answers, some haven't. As it's still ongoing, and we don't know how long it's going to go, there's only so much I can say.”The former United midfielder, who spent 12 years at Old Trafford between 2006 and 2018, admitted that the case had a personal dimension for him after experiencing some of the club's most painful title-race defeats against their Manchester rivals.“Certainly I've got my own questions about it, it's affected me personally in different ways over a period of time. But as the case is going now I don't know where that stands and how it's going to end up, so we'll just have to wait and see,” he added.“What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone's benefit is essential.”Carrick reflects on United's lost title racesCarrick was part of the United side that lost out to City in two Premier League title races, including the dramatic 2011-12 season when United finished level on points with their neighbours but missed out on the title on goal difference.Sergio Aguero's stoppage-time goal against Queens Park Rangers on the final day secured City's first Premier League crown and remains one of the competition's most memorable moments.Asked whether United should be awarded titles they missed out on if the case ultimately goes against City, Carrick said the emotional significance of winning a trophy could not simply be recreated later.“I think regardless of anything, a medal anyway, in any sport in history, I think later on you get the medal and it's proven at different times,” the Englishman said.“It's the moment that you strive for to win and achieve in that moment, so the medal here or there, not getting blase about it, but that doesn't bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don't win. That's essentially what we're all in it for.”An independent commission found City guilty of charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over nine seasons, from 2009-10 to 2017-18, along with three of four charges relating to their failure to cooperate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.United turn focus to Tottenham clashCarrick's comments came ahead of United's Premier League fixture against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. United, sitting 12th in the table, will face the bottom-placed side while dealing with several injury concerns.Wing-back Patrick Dorgu is expected to be sidelined for several weeks after picking up an injury during the international break, while defender Noussair Mazraoui is also a doubt.“It's a bit mixed really through the internationals,” Carrick said. “(Wing back) Patrick Dorgu came off and it looks like he'll be out probably for a number of weeks.”“(Defender) Noussair Mazraoui came off and took a knock. He's not quite right yet, we'll have to see how he is.”Carrick added that Carlos Baleba was improving, while Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Marcus Rashford had resumed limited training.
